roster.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
roster.outlook: Jaxon Smith-Njigba should once again be the centerpiece of Seattle's passing game in a big Week 5 clash against the 49ers. The star wideout posted a fine 5-76-0 receiving line against the Chargers this past Sunday, though he didn't get into the end zone for the first time this season. It's telling that despite his final stats being quite adequate, Smith-Njigba's targets, catches and yards were each a season-low mark in what has been a standout campaign thus far. San Francisco is allowing just 6.96 yards per target to wideouts though four weeks (fifth-best in the league), though Smith-Njigba has proven to be essentially matchup-proof since the beginning of last season.

roster.name: Saquon Barkley
roster.outlook: Saquon Barkley left Philadelphia's last game due to a hamstring ailment. While the injury is not considered serious, it remains to be seen whether Barkley will be able to suit up in London in Week 5 versus the Jags. If Barkley can play, he will face a stiff test, as Jacksonville is allowing just 74.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is second in the NFL. In addition, the Jags have given up just two rushing touchdowns through the first four games of the season.

roster.name: Colston Loveland
roster.outlook: Colston Loveland will look to build off a season-best performance as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Loveland commanded nine targets in Week 4 against the Jets, which allowed him to finish with six catches for 57 yards. The second-year tight end has now increased his yardage from zero to three to 31 to 57 in the first four games of the year. He'll aim to find the end zone for the first time of the campaign against a Packers defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against TEs so far this season.

roster.name: Jameson Williams
roster.outlook: Jameson Williams will look to build off a big outing as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. Williams had his best game of the year in Week 4 against the Panthers, bringing in six of eight targets for 102 yards. The speedster has still posted just a 16-229-0 receiving line to start the season, but he has seen eight or more targets in two games, which could bode well for his output. He'll also face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Parker Washington
roster.outlook: Parker Washington has recorded just 47 receiving yards on eight targets over Jacksonville's last two games after turning 18 targets into 181 yards over the preceding two games. Washington could have an easier time getting back on track in Week 5 if the Eagles are without top cornerback Quinyon Mitchell (knee). Philadelphia's secondary still has plenty of talent but hasn't been nearly as effective this year, allowing four touchdown catches to WRs after holding the position to six TDs in the entire 2025 regular season. Washington leads the Jaguars in all receiving categories and remains a fantasy WR2 at worst despite the recent hiccup.

roster.name: J.K. Dobbins
roster.outlook: J.K. Dobbins continues to struggle as the primary early-down back for the Broncos. In a Week 4 loss to the 49ers, he managed just 40 rushing yards on 11 carries. This marks the fourth straight game to begin the season he's failed to reach 50 rushing yards or get into the end zone. Dobbins' 3.5 yards per carry would be a career low; he's never had a mark below 4.6 in any year he's played at least eight games. The veteran RB has at least stayed healthy, but that hasn't led to much production. He'll try to get going in Week 5 against a Chargers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: KC Concepcion
roster.outlook: KC Concepcion and the Browns visit the Jets for a Week 5 showdown. The rookie receiver finished second on the team in receptions (5) and yardage (64), while his eight targets led the way in Cleveland's Week 4 victory. Concepcion also returned two punts for 10 yards, as it remains clear the Browns want the ball in his hands in a variety of ways for him to shine as a playmaker. However, he'll face a talented Jets secondary that allows 28.5 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks ninth in the league.

roster.name: Chase McLaughlin
roster.outlook: Chase McLaughlin is expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Buccaneers' Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. McLaughlin didn't attempt a field goal in the Week 4 loss to the Packers but made both of his point-after attempts. On the season, he's converted on all nine of his field-goal tries, including three from beyond 50 yards. McLaughlin could get fewer kicking chances with Jalon Daniels starting at quarterback for the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb), but the Cowboys remain a favorable matchup, allowing 8.5 kicking points per game this season.

roster.name: Emanuel Wilson
roster.outlook: Emanuel Wilson will look to build upon a big Week 4 performance when Seattle faces San Francisco in Week 5. Wilson led his team's backfield this past Sunday against the Chargers, posting a 21-81-1 line on the ground. Equally promising was his 3-39-1 line as a pass catcher after he logged zero receptions over the first three weeks of the campaign. With Jadarian Price (chest) on IR, Wilson figures to continue to work as Seattle's No. 1 RB, though the eventual return of Zach Charbonnet (knee) could shake up the backfield. Charbonnet isn't expected to be ready for Week 5, however, so Wilson will likely get plenty of work against the 49ers, who are middle-of-the-pack so far in giving up 17.4 fantasy points per game to running backs.

roster.name: Denzel Boston
roster.outlook: Denzel Boston and the Browns are on the road to take on the Jets in Week 5. He caught four of seven targets for a team-high 89 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 4. Boston tied for third in targets and continued to prove himself as a big-play option, generating 60 yards on one reception that helped set up a Browns' touchdown run. He'll face a strong Jets secondary that allows 28.5 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks ninth in the league.

roster.name: Jacoby Brissett
roster.outlook: Jacoby Brissett will aim to clean up his mistakes when Arizona hosts Detroit in Week 5. Brissett threw three interceptions against the Giants in Week 4 after getting picked off just once through his first three games of the season. The veteran quarterback has still been pretty productive with 818 passing yards, six touchdowns and 43 rushing yards (with one touchdown) overall this season. He next draws a juicy matchup against the Lions, who have given up the most fantasy points per game (32.7) to quarterbacks on the campaign.

roster.name: James Cook III
roster.outlook: James Cook will likely require volume to exploit a Rams defense when the Bills face them in their Week 5 Monday night affair. Cook has now scored in three straight games, but his workload was minimal in Week 4 against New England, rushing a season-low 12 times. The Rams have been stout against the run, not allowing a running back to score through four games and allowing just 3.9 yards per carry, and Cook's lack of involvement in the passing game further dampens the outlook. So long as Buffalo doesn't fall behind early and is forced to throw often, Cook remains stable, but Week 5 profiles as a night to temper lofty expectations.

roster.name: Chase Brown
roster.outlook: Chase Brown and the Bengals visit the 0-4 Dolphins for a Week 5 showdown. He had nine carries for 10 yards but caught all 11 of his targets for 71 yards during Cincinnati's 22-17 loss in Week 4. Brown set a career high in receptions with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) leaving in the first half, and with Tee Higgins (adductor) picking up a questionable tag, the running back could again get high volume through the air while still handling the bulk of carries. Miami's defense ranks last in fantasy points (29.7) and receiving TDs (4) allowed to the position, giving Brown a very favorable matchup.

roster.name: Nico Collins
roster.outlook: Nico Collins returned from a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury in Week 5 and reclaimed his customary spot as Houston's top receiver and a fantasy WR1. He scored twice against the Cowboys and has compiled 14 catches for 194 yards and three TDs in two appearances this season. Collins can be started with confidence in Week 5 against the Titans, who are allowing 167 receiving yards per game to wideouts. DeVonta Smith and Zay Flowers each compiled at least 117 yards and a TD against Tennessee's secondary.

roster.name: DeVonta Smith
roster.outlook: DeVonta Smith missed last game for the Eagles with a hamstring issue, and his status is very much up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. Philadelphia's passing offense struggled mightily without Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert, and the early departure of Saquon Barkley due to an injury of his own did not help matters. If Smith misses additional time, Dontayvion Wicks, Darius Cooper and rookie Makai Lemon will have some big shoes to fill. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.

roster.name: D'Andre Swift
roster.outlook: D'Andre Swift will seek to get back on track as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Swift rushed the ball 15 times for 58 yards and caught two targets for 16 yards against the Jets in Week 4, but he also lost a fumble and was stopped at the goal line twice. The veteran was outplayed by his younger counterpart, Kyle Monangai, who posted a 30-146-2 rushing line. Either way, Swift should still get plenty of usage against a Packers defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.

roster.name: Rome Odunze
roster.outlook: Rome Odunze will look to build off a big performance as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Odunze was on fire in Week 4 against the Jets with Tyson Bagent under center, bringing in six of seven targets for 94 yards. The starting wide receiver has now posted a 14-233-0 receiving line on the year, which leaves plenty of room to grow. He'll face a Green Bay defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 31.8 fantasy points per game to wide receivers.

roster.name: Christian Watson
roster.outlook: Christian Watson will remain a top option in Green Bay's passing game against the Bears in Week 5. Watson finished Week 4 at Tampa Bay with a quiet three catches for 47 yards, but Jordan Love threw for just 197 yards. The go-to wideout has now posted a 20-331-4 receiving line on 32 targets so far this campaign, and he's on pace for his first 1,000-yard season if he can stay healthy. Watson could have a tough task versus a Chicago defense that's ranked top five in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers so far this season.

roster.name: Justin Herbert
roster.outlook: Justin Herbert continues to struggle in offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The 28-year-old quarterback posted season lows with 189 passing yards and 6.1 yards per attempt in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks. Through four games, he has a career-low 59.7% completion rate and a weak 4:6 TD:INT. An ineffective running game, along with injuries to the offensive line and his wide receiver corps, have contributed to the team's 0-4 start, but Herbert has been the focal point of the offense's woes. He'll try to turn things around in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain, and which ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

roster.name: Matthew Golden
roster.outlook: Matthew Golden will look to do more as the Packers play the Bears in Week 5. Golden finished Week 4 against the Buccaneers with a season-low three catches for 21 yards, but he was able to salvage his performance with a touchdown. The second-year pass catcher remains a top option for quarterback Jordan Love, and he has an 18-274-2 receiving line through four games. Golden will be a major factor in Green Bay's success against their big rival, but he will face a Chicago defense that's ranked top five in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

roster.name: RJ Harvey
roster.outlook: RJ Harvey is coming off the best performance of his career as a pass catcher, posting a 10-68-0 line on 10 targets while adding 25 rushing yards on seven carries in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers. Denver trailed most of the game, which helped boost the second-year back's usage, but J.K. Dobbins' struggles in the early-down role are also opening the door for Harvey to log more touches in general, as his seven carries were also a season high. The eventual return of rookie Jonah Coleman from a high-ankle sprain could shake up the backfield further, but until then Harvey's arrow appears to be pointed up. He'll look to build on last week's effort in Week 5 against a Chargers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs..

roster.name: Eddy Pineiro
roster.outlook: Eddy Pineiro's leg could be key for the 49ers in Week 5 versus Seattle in a battle of tough defenses. Pineiro has been mostly asked to kick extra points this season, making 14 of 16 PAT tries while attempting just six field goals (and making four of them). He missed a 54-yard try against Denver this past Sunday, though it was blocked by the Broncos. There may not be many opportunities for Pineiro against the Seahawks, who are giving up the fifth-fewest points (18.3) in the league this season.

roster.name: George Pickens
roster.outlook: George Pickens has had back-to-back games with at least 75 yards receiving for the Cowboys. On the downside, Pickens was targeted just three times last game as compared to a staggering 21 targets for fellow wideout CeeDee Lamb. The targets are unlikely to be so lopsided in Week 5 versus the Bucs, but Pickens certainly appears to be playing second-fiddle to the aforementioned Lamb in 2026. Tampa Bay's defense has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.

roster.name: T.J. Hockenson
roster.outlook: T.J. Hockenson will look to build on a huge performance as the Vikings play New Orleans in Week 5. Hockenson finished Week 4 with a bang after starting the season quietly, catching all 13 of his targets for a whopping 119 yards. The veteran tight end could continue to be an outlet for quarterback Kyler Murray, especially with some struggles from the quarterback so far. The Saints have ranked bottom five against fantasy TEs so far this season.

roster.name: Malik Nabers
roster.outlook: Malik Nabers exploded last game for 112 yards and a touchdown to help the Giants to victory. Nabers snagged six passes on seven targets for a season-high in terms of receiving yardage. He and quarterback Jameis Winston finally appeared to be on the same page. In Week 5, Nabers and company will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass.  Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.

roster.name: Cam Skattebo
roster.outlook: Cam Skattebo has struggled to find room to roam for the Giants thus far this season. Skattebo rushed 18 times for 58 yards in the 36-24 win over the Cardinals last game. He is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry as teams dare the Giants to throw with backup quarterback Jameis Winston. In Week 5, Skattebo will face a rather stingy Washington run defense as well. The Commanders are allowing just 93.5 yards per tilt on the ground, which is sixth in the league. However, Washington did allow three rushing touchdowns last game versus the Colts.

roster.name: Bucky Irving
roster.outlook: Bucky Irving is expected to remain the Buccaneers' main offensive weapon in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Irving was largely ineffective against the Packers in a Week 4 loss, rushing for 61 yards on 16 carries. Additionally, the Oregon product was held without a target after accumulating 15 in Tampa Bay's first three games, suggesting Irving is likely in for less pass-catching opportunities while Jalon Daniels remains the starting quarterback. Irving could still thrive in Week 5 against a Cowboys defense that's given up 22.4 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.

roster.name: Tucker Kraft
roster.outlook: Tucker Kraft will seek to build on his best performance of the season as the Packers take on Chicago in Week 5. Kraft recorded a season-high six catches in Week 4 against the Buccaneers, which he converted for 42 yards and a touchdown. The star tight end has started the campaign with a 15-148-1 receiving line, which he could expand on well against Green Bay's biggest rival. Kraft will have a tough task against a Bears defense that's ranked top five against fantasy TEs across four games.

roster.name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
roster.outlook: Marvin Harrison heads into Arizona's Week 5 matchup against Detroit struggling to build chemistry with QB Jacoby Brissett. Though Harrison recorded a 12-yard touchdown reception in Week 4 against the Giants, that was his only catch on four targets. The third-year wideout has exceeded one reception just once through four games this season and has totaled only 12 targets, remarkably far behind the 44 targets fellow wideout Michael Wilson has logged. With that said, the Lions could provide a prime opportunity for Harrison to get back on track, as Detroit has surrendered 207.3 receiving yards per game to wideouts, third-worst in the league.

roster.name: Trevor Lawrence
roster.outlook: Trevor Lawrence is off to an inconsistent start this season, with seven touchdown passes in two home games but just one touchdown pass in two road games. The Jaguars are the nominal home team in Week 5 against the Eagles, but the game will be played in London at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium rather than in Jacksonville. Given Lawrence's struggles away from home coupled with a matchup against an Eagles defense that has allowed just four touchdown passes in as many games, this could be a week to look elsewhere at QB if a viable alternative is available on your bench or waiver wire. Jacksonville's passing game has enough upside for Lawrence to deliver a starter-level performance, but his floor is well below that.

roster.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
roster.outlook: Jacory Croskey-Merritt was stymied last game in a dismal loss for the Commanders. Bill had nine carries for a season-low 15 yards in the 30-13 defeat to the Colts. Even with Rachaad White sidelined due to injury, Croskey-Merritt could find little room to roam. Bill is struggling overall this season, averaging just 2.8 yards per tote. In Week 5, Washington will face a Giants run defense that has vastly improved from a season ago. New York is allowing 109 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the league. In addition, the G-Men have surrendered only two rushing touchdowns through four contests.

roster.name: Jordan Mason
roster.outlook: Jordan Mason will remain out for Week 5 as the Vikings travel to New Orleans. Mason hurt his thumb in Week 1 against the Packers, and he's been on IR since. The fifth-year running back will remain sidelined for at least the next week, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role.

roster.name: Harrison Mevis
roster.outlook: Harrison Mevis heads into the Rams' Week 5 matchup against Buffalo with a modest four field goals on the season. Four of those came in Week 3 against Denver, and Mevis missed a 48-yard try this past Sunday against Philadelphia. The second-year pro is a perfect 10-for-10 on point-after tries this year and has made all 49 of his PAT attempts in his career. Buffalo has yielded just six FG tries through four weeks, with kickers making five of those attempts.

roster.name: Braelon Allen
roster.outlook: Braelon Allen could be slated for bulk carries in Week 5 when the Jets face the Browns with Breece Hall's (quad) uncertain availability. Filling in for Hall in Week 4, Allen was the only Jet to receive a carry, putting him in line to potentially exploit a Cleveland defense that's allowed at least 82 yards to opposing lead backs in three straight weeks and an appealing 4.8 yards per carry. If Hall returns, he can't be guaranteed a full workload, lending flex appeal to Allen.

roster.name: Ollie Gordon II
roster.outlook: Ollie Gordon could be emerging in the Dolphins' backfield heading into a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals. With De'Von Achane (knee) out, Gordon ran for 100 yards on just nine carries in Week 4, vastly outperforming Jaylen Wright, while also scoring a touchdown for the second straight week. Touches figure to remain low if the Dolphins are forced to play from behind early, but facing a defense that's allowing 4.5 yards per carry could lead to steady yardage without high volume, and Gordon will remain an option near the goal line.

roster.name: Juwan Johnson
roster.outlook: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Johnson had another productive outing in the Week 4 loss to the Falcons, catching six of eight targets for 59 yards. He's now tallied 232 receiving yards through four contests this season, the fourth-most amongst tight ends. Johnson will likely continue to benefit from head coach Kellen Moore's pass-heavy offense that's averaged 45 pass attempts per game this year. Despite this, Johnson is in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Vikings defense that's given up just 7.7 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs.

roster.name: Jaylen Warren
roster.outlook: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers welcome the Colts to town in Week 5. He tallied 17 carries for 93 yards while catching three of six targets for 33 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss. Warren handled a massive workload for the second straight week with Rico Dowdle (toe) on the sidelines. There's a chance Dowdle remains out against Indianapolis, leaving Warren as the unquestioned lead back versus the Colts' 23rd-ranked defense, which has allowed 24.2 fantasy points per game to RBs.

roster.name: Zay Flowers
roster.outlook: Zay Flowers looks to continue his hot start in 2026 when the Ravens visit the Falcons in Week 5. He grabbed eight of 10 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown during Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4. The fourth-year wideout owns an 18-352-2 receiving line on 22 targets across three contests. However, if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is unable to suit up, Flowers will be catching passes from Tyler Huntley, who completed eight of nine passes for 63 yards in relief of Jackson. He'll have the added benefit of facing an Atlanta defense that allows 38.4 fantasy points per game (T-27th) to WRs and gave up eight receptions for 116 yards to Chris Olave.

roster.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
roster.outlook: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to return to dominance as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. Gibbs produced for fantasy managers in Week 4, but he still rushed 15 times for a season-low 46 yards with a touchdown, tacking on four catches for 31 yards. Either way, the superstar running back has found the end zone in every game this season, and he's surpassed 100 total yards in three of four games. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked top five against fantasy RBs this season.

roster.name: Jeremiyah Love
roster.outlook: Jeremiyah Love is dealing with an ankle injury, and his status is uncertain for Arizona's Week 5 matchup against Detroit. The rookie running back logged a full workload Week 4 against the Giants, finishing with 14 carries for 63 yards and one catch for minus-8 yards. Fantasy managers who roster Love will likely keep a close eye on the Cardinals' injury reports throughout the week to get a sense of his odds of playing in Week 5. If he does suit up, Love will face a Lions defense that allowed Carolina RB Chuba Hubbard to rumble for 122 rushing yards and two touchdowns in Week 4.

roster.name: Ladd McConkey
roster.outlook: Ladd McConkey failed to catch either of his targets in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, leaving the game early after aggravating a foot injury he picked up in practice during the week. The third-year wideout was already playing through a rib issue, and an absence of one or more games seems almost assured. The Chargers' passing game has struggled with or without him on the field, but if McConkey does miss time, Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris would become Justin Herbert's top downfield options in Week 5 against a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain.

roster.name: Joe Burrow
roster.outlook: Joe Burrow and the Bengals travel to take on the 0-4 Dolphins in Week 5. He completed 39 of 54 pass attempts for 428 yards with one TD and two INTs while rushing three times for six yards and another score during Cincinnati's 22-17 loss in Week 4. The Bengals leaned on Burrow while playing from behind most of the game, but with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) both questionable to suit up against Miami, they're hoping a better start will allow them to rely on the ground game a bit more. The Dolphins' defense is certainly beatable, allowing 21.2 fantasy points to QBs (T-18th) and 29.7 to RBs, which ranks dead last.

roster.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
roster.outlook: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns look to stay hot and earn a fourth consecutive victory against the Jets in a Week 5 road clash. He caught three of five targets for 27 yards and a touchdown during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 4. The second-year tight end now has three combined TDs over his last two outings. Fannin should once again be a featured target for Deshaun Watson versus the Jets' ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (10.2) to TEs. They have yet to surrender a TD to the position.

roster.name: DK Metcalf
roster.outlook: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Colts in a Week 5 clash between 2-2 teams. He caught five of nine targets for 115 yards during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. Metcalf turned in his best performance of the season by far while leading his team in receptions, yardage, and targets. He'll look to stay hot against a beatable Indianapolis secondary that allows 35.0 fantasy points per game (20th) to WRs.

roster.name: Cameron Dicker
roster.outlook: Cameron Dicker's volume increased for a second straight week in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, converting all three of his field-goal attempts and both of his PATs. While the team's offense continues to struggle, Justin Herbert is at least putting together longer drives, and during those two contests Dicker has gone 6-for-7 on FG tries with all of his attempts coming from inside 50 yards. He likely won't be able to squander many chances in Week 5 against a Broncos team allowing 23.5 points per game, 17th in the league.

roster.name: Brock Purdy
roster.outlook: Brock Purdy will look to help keep San Francisco's perfect record alive with a win over Seattle in Week 5. Purdy has been outstanding to the begin the campaign, completing 70% of his passes and recording an 11:1 TD:INT. He's also getting great protection from the offensive line, as he's yet to take a sack this season. The Seahawks could pose a stiff challenge, however, as they've collected seven sacks through five games and have allowed the fifth-lowest passer rating (76.2) in the league.

roster.name: Dalton Kincaid
roster.outlook: Dalton Kincaid faces an uphill battle for a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Rams in Week 5. He is coming off a season-low seven yards on two targets (one catch), and after a productive two-game start, has only five targets in Weeks 3 and 4. The Rams have defended tight ends at an elite level, allowing a mere 2.9 yards per target and only 85 total yards through four games.

roster.name: Deebo Samuel Sr.
roster.outlook: Deebo Samuel has been a versatile cog for the 49ers heading into a Week 5 matchup against Seattle. Samuel has scored three receiving TDs though four games, and he's also racked up 185 receiving yards, 74 rushing yads and 231 kick-return yards. The veteran wideout has drawn a modest 17 targets so far, but he's been very efficient in hauling in 14 of them. San Francisco may look to use Samuel creatively against a Seahawks defense that is allowing just 246.8 yards per game this season, fewest in the league.

roster.name: Rico Dowdle
roster.outlook: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Colts in a battle between 2-2 teams in Week 5. He missed his second consecutive game with a toe injury sustained in Week 2. Jaylen Warren accounted for 20 of 22 touches by running backs during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss, a pattern that would surely continue if Dowdle remains sidelined against Indianapolis. Monitor his practice participation leading up to a favorable matchup versus the Colts' 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (24.2) to RBs.

roster.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
roster.outlook: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to find the end zone again as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. St. Brown returned to a solid eight catches for 75 yards against the Panthers in Week 4, but he also broke his three-game touchdown streak. The star pass catcher has now totaled 31 receptions for 303 yards and five touchdowns this season. He'll take on a Cardinals defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Bijan Robinson
roster.outlook: Bijan Robinson is expected to continue leading Atlanta's offense during the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Robinson has excelled through the Falcons' first four games, averaging 153.5 total yards per game and scoring five touchdowns on 99 touches. He ranks second in the NFL in total yards and will likely remain the focal point of a Falcons offense that's averaged 40 points per game over their last two contests. Despite this, Robinson is in for a difficult Wek 5 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed just 19.1 fantasy points per game to RBs this year.

roster.name: Josh Allen
roster.outlook: Josh Allen brings a multi-touchdown streak into the Bills' Week 5 matchup at the Rams. Allen has provided multiple scores in each of Buffalo's first four games, throwing six scores while rushing for seven, though his yardage has topped 253 just once. The Rams, however, have allowed only one rushing touchdown and a mere 4.84 yards per pass attempt in what looks to be a battle of elite versus elite.

roster.name: Emeka Egbuka
roster.outlook: Emeka Egbuka will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Buccaneers' Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Egbuka was targeted just four times during the Week 4 loss to the Packers, his lowest mark of the season. While Baker Mayfield (thumb) remains sidelined and Jalon Daniels acts as the Buccaneers' signal caller, Egbuka may continue receiving less opportunities. However, he's in for a great Week 5 matchup against a Dallas defense that's given up 36.9 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

roster.name: DJ Moore
roster.outlook: DJ Moore continues to battle a shoulder issue as the Bills get set to travel in Week 5 to face the Rams. Moore exited Week 4's game against New England after aggravating the injury, his second early departure in four games. When playing an entire four quarters, Moore has dominated targets from Josh Allen, averaging nine looks. However, pairing injury concerns with the Rams' secondary not allowing an opposing receiver to top 50 yards, Moore could struggle in Week 5.

roster.name: Luther Burden III
roster.outlook: Luther Burden will aim to stay involved as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Burden tied his season high of 63 receiving yards in Week 4 against the Jets, and he's now recorded 60 or more yards in all but one game this season. The second-year wide receiver appears to be a pivotal part of Chicago's offense, and he could be a key piece towards a win in Tundratown. He'll face a Packers defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this campaign.

roster.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
roster.outlook: Kyle Pitts is expected to remain one of the Falcons' top pass catchers in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Pitts had his most productive game of the season in the Week 4 win over the Saints, catching all three of his targets for 47 yards. Despite this, he played just 50% of Atlanta's offensive snaps and has now logged an average of 2.3 targets per game, suggesting he may not be as involved in the team's offensive game plan as he has been in past years. Additionally, Pitts in in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed just 10.4 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

roster.name: Courtland Sutton
roster.outlook: Courtland Sutton was nearly invisible in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers, catching only one of six targets for a measly four yards. The veteran wideout remains firmly behind Jaylen Waddle on the depth chart, but the entire Denver offense is struggling under first-time play caller Davis Webb, and Sutton has produced a weak 9-86-0 line on 22 targets through four games. How long Sean Payton lets that situation last before reclaiming play-calling duties is an open question. Sutton will try to get going in Week 5 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: MarShawn Lloyd
roster.outlook: MarShawn Lloyd remains in the mix of Green Bay's backfield ahead of Week 5 against Chicago. Lloyd remained extremely inefficient on the ground in Week 4, rushing the ball seven times for 13 yards, but he did salvage his performance with five catches for 36 yards. The second-year running back looks to be in direct competition with Kaleb Johnson for carries as of late, but the Packers have utilized Lloyd in different ways even when Johnson has been more effective. Chicago has ranked 26th in yards per carry allowed (4.73) to RBs this season, which could give Lloyd the opening he needs to do more as a rusher.

roster.name: Brian Thomas Jr.
roster.outlook: Brian Thomas has just 25 receiving yards over Jacksonville's last two games after kicking off the season with consecutive 40-yard performances. The 2024 first-round pick has played fewer than 50% of snaps on offense while being outperformed by Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers. Thomas is too talented to overlook completely, but he's a risky flex option for Week 5 against the Eagles in London. The matchup would become more favorable if Eagles CB Quinyon Mitchell (knee) sits. Philadelphia is allowing 162 receiving yards per game to wide receivers.

roster.name: Kyle Monangai
roster.outlook: Kyle Monangai will look to shed a questionable tag after a huge performance as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Monangai dominated the Jets on the ground in Week 4 with 30 rushes for 146 yards and two touchdowns, but he also injured his thumb and is currently day-to-day. The second-year ball carrier's practice availability should dictate whether he's able to play in Chicago's rivalry debut of the 2026 season. If he's active, he'll face a Green Bay defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.

roster.name: Jake Ferguson
roster.outlook: Jake Ferguson had a two-game scoring streak snapped for the Cowboys. Ferguson managed three catches for just 11 yards in the 34-30 win over the Texans. Ferguson has just 12 catches for 83 yards through the first four games of the season, though has scored three times over that span. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.

roster.name: Cam Little
roster.outlook: Cam Little made all three of his field-goal attempts in Jacksonville's Week 4 win over the Bengals. The big-legged kicker has yet to miss from inside 50 yards and has tremendous range, as Little made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season and narrowly missed a 70-yard attempt this season. Little remains a viable fantasy starter as usual in Week 5 against an Eagles team that's allowing 23.3 points per game but has given up only six successful field goals through four games. This game will be played at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, where Spencer Shrader and Drew Stevens combined to make all five of their field-goal attempts in Week 4.

roster.name: Tyler Shough
roster.outlook: Tyler Shough is expected to lead the Saints' offense into the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Despite a loss in Week 4, Shough remained productive, throwing for 286 yards and a touchdown with no turnovers. The second-year pro is now averaging a whopping 45 pass attempts per game, suggesting he'll remain productive for fantasy purposes as the season progresses. Despite this, he's in for a very tough Week 5 matchup against a Vikings defense that's allowed just 15.7 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, the best mark in the NFL.

roster.name: Ja'Marr Chase
roster.outlook: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals travel to face the winless Dolphins in Week 5. He caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in Week 4 before leaving Cincinnati's 22-17 loss with a concussion in the second quarter. Chase was evaluated for the injury after his facemask was pulled following a catch, and he'll have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol before he can return to practice and play in the upcoming contest versus Miami. If he is indeed active, Chase will be going up against the Dolphins, who rank third in fewest fantasy points allowed (22.2) to WRs.

roster.name: Drake London
roster.outlook: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. London has excelled since the return of Michael Penix in Week 3, catching 14 of 16 targets for 290 yards across his last two contests. With Penix at the helm, London has averaged a whopping 6.6 receptions and 98.5 yards per game, suggesting that he'll remain one of fantasy's top wideouts as the season progresses. Additionally, London is in for a terrific matchup against a Ravens secondary that's allowed 37.9 fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.

roster.name: Breece Hall
roster.outlook: Breece Hall is uncertain to face the Browns in the Jets' Week 5 matchup due to a quad injury. He missed Week 4 with the issue, and when healthy, he was limited to 32 or fewer yards in his last two outings. Should he suit up, it's possible he'd be eased into his return and share snaps with Braelon Allen, but it's a favorable spot if a normal workload can be anticipated. While Cleveland has yet to allow a running back to score, they're allowing 4.8 yards per carry, with the last three lead backs all reaching at least 82 yards.

roster.name: Quinshon Judkins
roster.outlook: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns visit the Jets in Week 5, looking for their fourth consecutive win. He had his best performance of 2026 in Week 4, rushing 17 times for 53 yards and his first TD of the season while catching six of seven targets for 43 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 victory. No other back recorded more than two carries, and Judkins led the team in receptions and tied for third in targets. Up next is a Jets defense that allows 28.3 fantasy points per game to RBs, which ranks 30th.

roster.name: Lamar Jackson
roster.outlook: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens travel to face the Falcons on Sunday Night Football in Week 5. Prior to missing the entire second half of Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4, the two-time MVP threw for 222 yards (15-for-20) with two TDs and no INTs while rushing twice for 20 yards. Jackson was well on his way to a stellar outing with his team up 24-7 at halftime, but an ankle injury forced him out early and has him in jeopardy of missing the upcoming road tilt in Atlanta. Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that the Ravens are uncertain of Jackson's status for Week 5, and if he's unable to suit up, Tyler Huntley will get the nod at quarterback.

roster.name: David Montgomery
roster.outlook: David Montgomery has plodded to 2.7 yards per carry and has failed to find the end zone since scoring three TDs in Week 1, his Texans debut. Fellow Houston RB Woody Marks has scored twice during Montgomery's three-game touchdown drought. Montgomery and Marks will likely split carries again in Week 5 against the Titans, who are allowing 100 rushing yards per game to RBs, though Tennessee is giving up only 3.6 yards per carry. If Houston's defense can recapture last season's elite form and stifle the underwhelming Titans offense, Montgomery could get enough volume to wear down Tennessee's defense and make up for a lack of quality with quantity. With Houston's running game stuck in first gear, Montgomery is an unexciting flex candidate for Week 5.

roster.name: Carnell Tate
roster.outlook: Carnell Tate broke out in Week 4 against the Ravens, recording 145 receiving yards after totaling just 123 yards over his first three games for the Titans. The rookie fourth-overall pick has been limited by the struggles of second-year QB Cam Ward, who is averaging just 182 passing yards per game. Tate is likely to match up frequently with top Texans CB Derek Stingley in Week 5, but Stingley and company have allowed the second-most catches (60), receiving yards (830), and touchdown receptions (six) to wide receivers. With Tate trending in the right direction, he's a high-upside flex option for Week 5 as the promising rookie continues to search for his first NFL touchdown.

roster.name: Sam LaPorta
roster.outlook: Sam LaPorta will look to build on a season-best showing as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. LaPorta impressed even in a Week 4 loss to Carolina, reeling in eight of 13 targets for 84 yards and a touchdown. The fourth-year tight end has now registered a 22-228-2  receiving line this season, and he remains a consistent option for Jared Goff, especially in important situations. LaPorta will face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Jason Myers
roster.outlook: Jason Myers has had a quiet campaign so far with Seattle on tap to host San Francisco in Week 5. After attempting a career-high 48 field goals in 2025, Myers has had just five FG tries so far this season, making all of them. He's been more active kicking extra points, making 12 of 13 PATs. Perhaps Myers will be relied upon more versus the 49ers, who have allowed just five extra-point tries as opposed to nine FG attempts so far in 2026.

roster.name: Makai Lemon
roster.outlook: Makai Lemon saw a career-high six targets last game for the Eagles. With DeVonta Smith shelved due to a hamstring ailment, Lemon finished with the second-most targets on the team behind Darius Cooper.  However, the Philadelphia passing game struggled mightily overall, with no wideout gaining more than 33 yards through the air. While Smith should remain sidelined for Week 5, it remains to be seen how the targets will be divided between Lemon, Cooper and Dontayvion Wicks. Nevertheless, an intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 against the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.

roster.name: Romeo Doubs
roster.outlook: Romeo Doubs has an ascending role in the Patriots' passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Raiders. He collected a season-high nine targets in Week 4, and while it resulted in just six catches and 58 yards, he found the end zone twice. Las Vegas will rush the passer, which has troubled Drake Maye. The secondary is allowing 8.2 yards per target to wideouts, so Doubs can capitalize on whatever volume he receives.

roster.name: Woody Marks
roster.outlook: Woody Marks takes a two-game touchdown streak into the Texans' Week 5 trip to Tennessee, though he has been out-touched 54-35 by David Montgomery in Houston's backfield. Marks has pulled within one touchdown of Montgomery this season, and neither running back has been efficient behind Houston's struggling offensive line, as Marks is averaging 3.1 yards per carry to Montgomery's 2.7. The Titans are giving up 100 yards per game on the ground to RBs, but Marks' position on the short end of a backfield platoon makes him a deep-league flex candidate at best for Week 5.

roster.name: Jared Goff
roster.outlook: Jared Goff will remain a high-volume option as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. No matter the outcome of each game so far, Goff has delivered consistent output, and Week 4 against the Panthers was no different. The veteran quarterback recorded season-high totals in completions, pass attempts and passing yards, completing 32 of 52 passes for 412 yards and one touchdown in what was an eventual loss. He's now thrown for 250 or more yards in his last three games, and he's yet to commit a turnover this year. Goff will face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 28th against fantasy quarterbacks this season.

roster.name: CeeDee Lamb
roster.outlook: CeeDee Lamb is coming off a game for the ages. Lamb was targeted a staggering 21 times en route to an absurd 17 catches for 189 yards and a touchdown in the comeback win over the Texans. It was the third-straight 100-yard outing of the season for Lamb, and he scored for the fourth time in four contests. Following this outing, Lamb leads the NFL in receiving yards and receptions, and is tied for third in the NFL with four receiving scores. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.

roster.name: Justin Jefferson
roster.outlook: Justin Jefferson will aim to make a return for Minnesota's Week 5 clash at New Orleans. Jefferson sat out of the Vikings' Week 4 win over the Dolphins with an ankle injury, but the hope is that his absences will be limited to that game. The star pass catcher has totaled a quieter 13-179-2 receiving line over his first two-plus games, so he'll look to make a bang if he does return to action. The Saints have ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this season, which could provide everything Jefferson needs to deliver.

roster.name: Garrett Wilson
roster.outlook: Garrett Wilson seeks a rebound in Week 5 when the Jets face the Browns. After collecting seven or more targets in each of his first three games, Wilson bottomed out with only four looks in Week 4, finishing with a season-low 27 yards. Cleveland's secondary has allowed at least 291 passing yards in each of the last two weeks, and three opposing wideouts have topped 70 yards. With his usual volume, Wilson appears to be in a favorable Week 5 spot.

roster.name: Javonte Williams
roster.outlook: Javonte Williams scored three times in the second half of the last game for the Cowboys, leading a thrilling comeback victory over the Texans. Williams is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote this season, but has six combined touchdowns through four outings. He has also made his presence felt in the passing game with 15 receptions over that span. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been stellar against the run in 2026. The Bucs are allowing just 78.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL. In addition, Tampa Bay has yielded just one rushing touchdown through four games.

roster.name: Bhayshul Tuten
roster.outlook: Bhayshul Tuten has recorded at least 88 scrimmage yards in three of the first four games of his second season with the Jaguars. The 2025 fourth-round pick has thrived in the lead role, establishing himself as an every-week fantasy RB2. He'll face an Eagles defense in Week 5 that's allowing 106 rushing yards per game to RBs and just surrendered a pair of late rushing scores to the Rams' Kyren Williams in a Week 4 loss. Tuten and the Jaguars will have a 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff Sunday in Week 5 when they face the Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

roster.name: Tyler Warren
roster.outlook: Tyler Warren has emerged with a consistent role as a short outlet for Colts QB Daniel Jones. Warren has caught 23 of 27 targets for 130 yards and two TDs, averaging almost six catches per game but just 5.7 yards per catch. His floor is high enough to be trusted as a weekly fantasy starter at TE, as Warren leads the Colts in catches and is one target shy of Josh Downs' team-leading total. Week 5 at Pittsburgh is no exception, even though the Steelers are tied for the fourth-fewest catches allowed to TEs with 13. Two of those 13 receptions have resulted in touchdowns.

roster.name: Dak Prescott
roster.outlook: Dak Prescott crossed the 300-yard passing mark last game for the Cowboys for the first time in 2026. Prescott actually threw for 335 yards in the thrilling comeback win over the Texans. More than half of the yards came via CeeDee Lamb, as the duo combined for a staggering 17 of Dak's 32 completions. Dak has eight passing scores and just one interception through four games. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.

roster.name: Mike Evans
roster.outlook: Mike Evans seems likely to continue playing through an injury to his ribs for San Francisco's Week 5 matchup against the Seahawks. The veteran wideout toughed out the injury in Week 4 and posted a 5-76-0 receiving line against a tough Broncos secondary. That receiving yardage was a season-high mark for Evans, as were his eight targets. Seattle could pose a significant challenge to the 49ers' receiving corps, however, as the Seahawks have yielded just 12.8 fantasy points per game to wideouts this season -- third-fewest in the NFL.

roster.name: Michael Wilson
roster.outlook: Michael Wilson has settled in atop Arizona's WR depth chart heading into a Week 5 tilt against the Lions. Wilson caught seven passes on 13 targets for 95 yards against the Giants in Week 4, leading or co-leading the Cardinals in all three categories. He's drawn a whopping 30 targets over his past two contests, making it clear that QB Jacoby Brissett sees him as the top option among the team's wideouts. Wilson could be in store for a big game against a Detroit defense that has yielded 28.3 fantasy points per game to wide receivers, third-most in the league.

roster.name: Caleb Williams
roster.outlook: Caleb Williams is set to miss another game as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is set to get the start again versus a Packers defense that gave up 148 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions to Buccaneers rookie Jalon Daniels in Week 4.

roster.name: Chris Godwin Jr.
roster.outlook: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top weapons in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Godwin was targeted a season-high seven times in the Week 4 loss to the Packers, catching six of them for just 31 yards. The veteran wideout may actually benefit from Jalon Daniels acting as Tampa Bay's starting quarterback while Baker Mayfield (thumb) is sidelined, as Godwin could act as the rookie's safety blanket. Additionally, Godwin is in for a good Week 5 matchup against a Dallas defense that's allowed five receiving touchdowns to WRs through four contests this year.

roster.name: Jordan Addison
roster.outlook: Jordan Addison will aim to do more as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Addison logged just four catches for 52 yards in Week 4 against the Dolphins, which was a bit of a disappointment given that Justin Jefferson (ankle) was inactive. Quarterback Kyler Murray also seemed to have built a connection with T.J. Hockenson against Miami, making it less likely that Addison will produce when Jefferson inevitably returns. The Saints have ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this campaign.

roster.name: Mark Andrews
roster.outlook: Mark Andrews and the Ravens are on the road for the first time since the season opener to face the Falcons in Week 5. He corralled five of six targets for 27 yards and his first touchdown of the season in Baltimore's Week 4 win. Andrews has yet to top 50 yards receiving through four outings to date, and that trend could continue if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is unable to play on Sunday Night Football. The veteran tight end will aim to find paydirt for the second straight week against Atlanta's 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (15.9) per game to the position.

roster.name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
roster.outlook: Ka'imi Fairbairn connected on all three of his Week 4 field-goal attempts, improving to 7-for-8 this season. Houston's excellent kicker could be busy in Week 5 against the Titans, whose nine made field goals allowed are tied for fifth-most in the NFL. Fairbairn has established himself as one of the busiest and most accurate kickers in the league, which is an excellent combination for fantasy purposes. He remains a set-and-forget fantasy starter.

roster.name: Puka Nacua
roster.outlook: Puka Nacua appears to be past his early-season injury woes as the Rams prepare to host Buffalo in Week 5. The star wideout missed Weeks 2 and 3 due to a hip/groin issue, but he returned this past Sunday against the Eagles and put up a 9-125-0 receiving line on 12 targets while adding a two-yard rushing touchdown. Nacua logged a 90% percent offensive snap share in the contest, so it doesn't appear that he is going to be inhibited by the injury, at least in terms of playing time, moving forward. The Bills present a good matchup on paper, as they've given up the fourth-most fantasy points (27.8) to wideouts so far this season.

roster.name: Ashton Jeanty
roster.outlook: Ashton Jeanty continues to bolster his lackluster rushing numbers with big production through the air. In the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, the second-year RB managed just 58 rushing yards on 15 carries, but he added six catches for 68 yards on a season-high eight targets. Jeanty's 3.4 yards per carry and zero TDs on the ground through four weeks are a concern, but his 19-165-2 line on 24 targets softens the blow. He'll take on a Patriots defense in Week 5 that ranks 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Trey McBride
roster.outlook: Trey McBride enters Arizona's Week 5 matchup against Detroit coming off his quietest performance of the season. While the star tight end logged a healthy 12 targets and seven catches against the Giants in Week 4, he finished with just 31 receiving yards. It's a testament to McBride's excellence that such a stat line represents a downturn by his standards, and he'll have a good chance of bouncing back against the Lions. Detroit has allowed a whopping 19.2 fantasy points per game to tight ends so far this season, by far the most in the league.

roster.name: Tee Higgins
roster.outlook: Tee Higgins and the Bengals are on the road to take on Miami's third-ranked defense against wide receivers in Week 5. He erupted for 11 catches and 157 yards on 16 targets during Cincinnati's Week 4 loss. With Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) exiting in the second quarter, Joe Burrow relied heavily on Higgins, as he paced the team in yardage and targets while tying for the lead in receptions. Unfortunately for the Bengals, Higgins sustained an adductor injury in the final minutes of the game, leaving his status questionable for Week 5.

roster.name: Drake Maye
roster.outlook: Drake Maye will look to carry momentum in Week 5 when the Patriots face the Raiders. After a dismal 1:6 TD:INT ratio through three games, Maye provided a season-high 269 yards and three touchdowns while adding 54 yards on eight rushes in Week 4 against Buffalo. Las Vegas is surrendering a 7:4 TD:INT ratio through four games, with six of those touchdowns coming in the last two weeks, suggesting Maye can provide the 2025 version expected by his fantasy managers in Week 5.

roster.name: TreVeyon Henderson
roster.outlook: TreVeyon Henderson will seek chunk plays in the Patriots' Week 5 matchup against a vulnerable Raiders run defense. Henderson had one more rush than Rhamondre Stevenson in this shared backfield in Week 4 but converted his 14 carries into only 42 yards. Henderson has not been a factor in the passing game, catching just one ball on the season. Las Vegas is allowing 4.97 yards per carry and has been picked apart by Kenneth Walker and Omarion Hampton, so Henderson appears set up for an ideal opportunity at a few long runs even if the volume won't be high.

roster.name: Tony Pollard
roster.outlook: Tony Pollard is averaging 61 scrimmage yards per game and scored his first touchdown of the season in Week 4 against the Ravens, though that wasn't enough to keep the Titans from dropping to 0-4. In Week 5, Tennessee hosts the AFC South rival Texans, who are also 0-4. The Titans should manage to stay within striking distance and give Pollard his full workload on the ground, though Houston has held RBs to just 91 scrimmage yards per game. Pollard is a high-floor, low-ceiling flex play as usual for Week 5 given his role as the lead back in a struggling Titans offense that's averaging the fewest yards and second-fewest points per game.

roster.name: Brandon Aubrey
roster.outlook: Brandon Aubrey missed two field goals last game for Dallas. Such a sensational headline needs explanation, though, as both of Aubrey's misses came from over 60 yards away. Aubrey had a 62-yarder blocked, and missed a 65-yarder wide left. Otherwise, Aubrey connected on two field goals from 50 yards and in, while also making all four of his extra points. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay squad allowing 24.0 points per clash, which is tied for 19th in the NFL.

roster.name: Travis Hunter
roster.outlook: Travis Hunter hasn't touched the ball on offense for the Jaguars since Week 1. He played every defensive snap in Week 4 and is focusing primarily on playing cornerback rather than wide receiver. Hunter is a fantasy non-factor except in formats that reward his defensive contributions. Jacksonville will face the Eagles in Week 5 in London, where Hunter showcased his upside on offense last season with eight catches for 101 yards and a TD against the Rams. Don't expect a repeat performance anytime soon, if ever.

roster.name: Aaron Jones Sr.
roster.outlook: Aaron Jones will remain a high-usage option as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Jones saw a big workload in Week 4 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 20 times for 94 yards and recording four catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield shouldn't change with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Saints defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy RBs this campaign.

roster.name: Khalil Shakir
roster.outlook: Khalil Shakir maintains a steady role out of the slot for Buffalo as they prepare to face the Rams in Week 5. Shakir is coming off a season-high 82 yards in Week 4, his third game with at least six targets. His workload is independent of DJ Moore's shoulder status. Shakir will either garner more targets if Moore is out, or benefit from the attention Moore usually draws. However, the Rams defense hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 50 yards, suggesting Shakir is a risky floor and limited ceiling option.

roster.name: Isaiah Likely
roster.outlook: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in targets last game. Likely saw a staggering 12 balls thrown his way en route to seven catches for 66 yards in the win over Arizona. However, fellow tight end Theo Johnson stole a touchdown from him. Still, Likely's renewed usage with quarterback Jameis Winston under center was a pleasant surprise, as Likely only had five targets in the prior game versus Tennessee. A tasty matchup lurks in Week 5 versus Washington. The Commanders defense has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.
