roster.name: Jonathan Taylor
roster.outlook: Jonathan Taylor has three multi-TD performances through four games and is averaging 88 rushing yards per game heading into the Colts' Week 5 trip to Pittsburgh. The Steelers rank among the 10 most generous defenses against RBs, allowing 138 scrimmage yards and one TD per game to the position. Taylor remains locked in as a fantasy RB1 while working as the focal point of the Colts' offense, which lacked talent at wide receiver even before injuries further depleted that position. His 26 scrimmage touchdowns since the start of last season are the most in the NFL over that span.

roster.name: Derrick Henry
roster.outlook: Derrick Henry and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 5 clash against the Falcons. He tallied 23 carries for 73 yards and one touchdown while catching both of his targets for six yards during Baltimore's Week 4 victory. Henry notched his seventh rushing TD of the season and now has at least one score in all four outings. With Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status up in the air, Henry should continue to be the focal point of the Ravens' offense versus Atlanta's ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.9) per game to RBs.

roster.name: Brock Bowers
roster.outlook: Brock Bowers shook off an illness to once again be the Raiders' top receiving option in a Week 4 loss to Kansas City. He caught six of 11 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown, finding the end zone for a second straight game after missing the first two weeks of the year while completing his recovery from knee surgery. The star tight end is the most dangerous weapon in Kirk Cousins' arsenal, and he's likely to continue getting double-digit targets on a weekly basis while posting elite numbers. Bowers faces his toughest test of the season so far in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to TEs in 2026.

roster.name: Davante Adams
roster.outlook: Davante Adams is coming off a quiet performance as the Rams prepare to host the Bills in Week 5. Against Philadelphia in Week 4, Adams was held to four catches for 32 yards. That was a substantial downturn after Adams averaged 7.5 catches and 166 yards over the previous two contests, though he still got a healthy nine targets against the Eagles. It has to be mentioned that star wideout Puka Nacua returned to action in Week 4 and posted a 9-125-0 line, while Adams' big performances the previous two weeks took place in games Nacua missed due to injury. Both WRs could find success against the Bills, who have allowed the fourth-most receiving yards to wideouts this year.

roster.name: Terry McLaurin
roster.outlook: Terry McLaurin missed last game for the Commanders due to a hamstring injury. McLaurin allegedly pushed hard to play, though, meaning he could very well return to the field in Week 5 versus the Giants. He also could have his starting quarterback Jayden Daniels back under center. New York has been stingy against the pass in 2026 thus far, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL. Likewise, the G-Men are tied for the league-lead with six picks.

roster.name: Jalen Hurts
roster.outlook: Jalen Hurts tossed two touchdowns last game for the Eagles. Unfortunately, he threw for just 93 yards in the 24-20 loss to the Rams. Hurts was missing DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert in the passing game, while Saquon Barkley left early due to an injury of his own, so Hurts cannot shoulder all the blame for this meager performance. Still, he has thrown for less than 250 yards combined in the last two contests. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags, though. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.

roster.name: Michael Pittman Jr.
roster.outlook: Michael Pittman and the Steelers host the receiver's former team when the Colts come to town in Week 5. He hauled in two of four targets for 15 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss, giving him a 7-89-0 receiving line on 12 targets across three contests. It's been a slow start for Pittman in his debut season for the Steelers, but Week 5 offers a shot at some payback against the team that drafted him in 2020. Indianapolis' defense ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (35.0) to WRs, a matchup that could help Pittman's chemistry with Aaron Rodgers.

roster.name: Wan'Dale Robinson
roster.outlook: Wan'Dale Robinson takes a two-game touchdown streak into Tennessee's Week 5 home game against the Texans, but he's averaging just 31 receiving yards per game as a Titan after coming over from the Giants in free agency. Houston has been surprisingly poor at defending wide receivers, allowing the second-most catches (60), receiving yards (830), and TDs (six) to the position. Robinson's inconsistent usage in a low-octane passing game makes him hard to trust, but he's a viable flex option for Week 5 given the Texans' struggles against his position.

roster.name: Quentin Johnston
roster.outlook: Quentin Johnston saw only two targets in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, but he was able to turn one of them into a 44-yard gain for his only catch. The season-low volume was especially disappointing given that Ladd McConkey left the game early with a foot injury. The passing game as a whole is struggling, and Johnston could end up getting passed on the depth chart by Tre' Harris if he doesn't begin to make a more consistent impact. Johnston will try to earn more look from Justin Herbert in Week 5 against a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs, but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks including Patrick Surtain.

roster.name: Michael Mayer
roster.outlook: Michael Mayer was busy in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, turning a season-high 10 targets into eight catches for 82 yards. The additional volume came after wide receiver Jalen Nailor left the game with a concussion, forcing Kirk Cousins to lean even more heavily on his tight end duo of Mayer and Brock Bowers to move the chains. Even with a healthy Bowers back in action the last two weeks, Mayer has delivered an 11-114-1 line on 13 targets. However, he'll struggle to maintain that pace in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to TEs in 2026.

roster.name: Keenan Allen
roster.outlook: Keenan Allen missed the Colts' Week 4 win over the Commanders due to a groin injury. If the 34-year-old WR is cleared to return in Week 5, he could play a prominent role opposite Josh Downs in a Colts WR room that remains without Alec Pierce (heel), who is on IR. Concerns about Allen's injury and performance limit his viability to deeper formats, even against a Steelers secondary that's giving up 149 receiving yards per game to wide receivers. Allen snapped a 12-game touchdown drought in the Colts' Week 3 win over Houston.

roster.name: Christian McCaffrey
roster.outlook: Christian McCaffrey will look to reach the end zone again for San Francisco in a Week 5 NFC West clash against the Seahawks. McCaffrey has scored at least one touchdown in three straight games and has four rushing TDs on the season. The scoring has helped keep his fantasy value high despite the fact that he's averaging a modest 16.5 touches per game so far after leading the NFL with 24.3 touches per game last season. Seattle has yielded just 3.35 yards per carry and one total rushing touchdown to running backs this season, but they've been more vulnerable through the air, allowing two receiving scores and an 88.5% catch rate to the position.

roster.name: Omarion Hampton
roster.outlook: Omarion Hampton scored a touchdown for the third time in four games during the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, but his role in the backfield continues to slip. The second-year back's nine carries and 11 touches were season lows for a spark for his unit. Hampton has still been the most productive of the trio this season with 267 scrimmage yards and three rushing TDs, but his 4.0 yards per carry trails Mitchell's, while Keaton Mitchell handled 15 touches and Kimani Vidal got seven, indicating that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is moving toward a full-blown committee as he searches 4.6 mark. Hampton will try to re-establish himself as the clear No. 1 on the depth chart in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Chris Olave
roster.outlook: Chris Olave is expected to lead New Orleans' receiving corps again in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Olave has been spectacular through the Saints' first four games this season, catching 35 of 48 targets for 491 yards (second in the NFL) and a touchdown. He's expected to continue benefitting from head coach Kellen Moore's pass-heavy offense, which has led to ample opportunities for Olave this season. Despite this, Olave could struggle in Week 5 against a tough Vikings secondary that's given up just 30.1 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

roster.name: Kyren Williams
roster.outlook: Kyren Williams enters the Rams' Week 5 matchup against the Bills with plenty of momentum. Williams totaled 147 yards and two touchdowns in a comeback win over Philadelphia in Week 4, pushing him up to four total TDs on the season. The star running back has logged at least 80 rushing yards in three straight games, and he's averaged 68.5 receiving yards across his past two contests. Buffalo has yielded 22.2 fantasy points per game to running backs so far, sixth-most in the NFL.

roster.name: Jaylen Waddle
roster.outlook: Jaylen Waddle scored his first touchdown with the Broncos in a Week 4 loss to the 49ers, but it was overall another disappointing performance from the former Dolphin. Waddle has recorded double-digit targets only once in four games to begin the season, leading to a modest 16-185-1 line on 26 looks from Bo Nix. That's still better numbers than Courtland Sutton, and the issue seems to be the overall struggles of the offense under first-time play caller Davis Webb. How long Sean Payton lets that situation last before reclaiming those duties is an open question for Denver. Waddle will try to hit paydirt again in Week 5 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Jayden Daniels
roster.outlook: Jayden Daniels could return in Week 5 for the Commanders from a dislocated elbow. Backup quarterback Marcus Mariota left Washington's last game with a knee injury, which could hasten the need for Daniels to return versus the Giants. if neither quarterback can suit up, seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis would get the nod. The defense for the Giants looks totally revamped in 2026, allowing 205.3 yards per tilt through the air, which is 10th in the league. The Giants are tied for the league-lead with six interceptions.

roster.name: George Kittle
roster.outlook: George Kittle could again be a key component of San Francisco's offense in Week 5 against Seattle. Kittle has scored a touchdown in three straight games, and he got into the end zone on a game-sealing 56-yard reception in Week 4 versus the Broncos. The veteran tight end enters the clash against Seattle with 244 receiving yards on the season, third-most among NFL tight ends. With that said, the Seahawks' defense has given up the fourth-fewest receiving yards to tight ends, so Kittle has his work cut out for him in Week 5.

roster.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
roster.outlook: Rhamondre Stevenson continues to share work in the Patriots backfield ahead of an inviting Week 5 matchup against the Raiders. He amassed 13 carries in Week 4, one fewer than TreVeyon Henderson's 14, but Stevenson found the end zone while catching three passes for the third time in four weeks. Las Vegas is allowing 4.97 yards per carry and was just solved by Kansas City's Kenneth Walker for 177 yards, so while split work will limit Stevenson's ceiling, his continued involvement as a pass-catcher paired with double-digit carries can result in fantasy-worthy production in Week 5.

roster.name: Stefon Diggs
roster.outlook: Stefon Diggs led the Commanders in targets and receptions last game. With Terry McLaurin sidelined due to a hamstring issue, Diggs managed five catches on nine targets. However, he could only muster 35 yards in the dismal 30-13 loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, which would certainly be a boost for Diggs, regardless of whether McLaurin also suits up. New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, though, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.

roster.name: Rachaad White
roster.outlook: Rachaad White missed Washington's last game due to a shoulder issue, leaving his status in question for Week 5 versus the Giants. An argument can be made that White has been more productive than fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt in 2026, though that point may be moot as long as White is sidelined. Austin Ekeler will be the backup to Bill if White remains shelved. In Week 5, Washington will face a Giants run defense that has vastly improved from a season ago. New York is allowing 109 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the league. In addition, the G-Men have surrendered only two rushing touchdowns through four contests.

roster.name: Josh Downs
roster.outlook: Josh Downs disappointed with 16 receiving yards against Washington's vulnerable secondary in Week 4 after notching at least 72 yards in each of the Colts' previous two games. Downs remains the de facto No. 1 WR for the Colts, as Alec Pierce (knee) is still on IR heading into a Week 5 road game at Pittsburgh. The Steelers are allowing 149 receiving yards per game to wideouts and traded starting CB Joey Porter to Dallas prior to Week 4. Downs is well-positioned to shake off his Week 4 dud and deliver as a solid Week 5 flex play.

roster.name: Kyler Murray
roster.outlook: Kyler Murray will look to do more as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. In his second full start of the year, Murray completed 27 of 37 passes for 247 yards, but he was unable to find the end zone. The veteran quarterback also now holds a 1:2 TD:INT through his three appearances this season, so he'll need to do more for Minnesota to lock him down as a long-term option. The Saints have ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy quarterbacks this season.

roster.name: Jake Bates
roster.outlook: Jake Bates will aim to stay perfect as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. Bates logged his best game of the season in Week 4 against the Panthers, nailing all four of his field-goal attempts and converting two XPAs. The second-year kicker has now gone a perfect 21-for-21 on boots (seven field goals, 14 extra points) this season. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked top 10 against fantasy kickers.

free_agents.name: Matthew Stafford
free_agents.outlook: Matthew Stafford will look to clean things up in the turnover department when the Rams host Buffalo in Week 5. Stafford was picked off twice and didn't throw any touchdowns in Week 4 against Philadelphia, but he also threw for 317 yards and led Los Angeles to a comeback victory. Still, Stafford has recorded a mediocre 6:6 TD:INT through four games, with the pickoff total nearly reaching the eight interceptions he tossed across 17 regular-season contests during his MVP campaign last year. The Bills have given up 10 passing touchdowns and have picked off just two passes this year, so Week 5 may be a good opportunity for Stafford to get back on track.

free_agents.name: Dallas Goedert
free_agents.outlook: Dallas Goedert missed last game for the Eagles with a knee issue, and his status is very much up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. Philadelphia's passing offense struggled mightily without Goedert and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith, and the early departure of Saquon Barkley due to an injury of his own did not help matters. If Goedert misses additional time, Zach Ertz would be the next man up.  An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Jakobi Meyers
free_agents.outlook: Jakobi Meyers has been efficient with his opportunities for the Jaguars, catching 13 of 15 targets for 165 yards and two touchdowns heading into a Week 5 trip to London to face the Eagles. His usage has fluctuated in a Jacksonville passing game with many mouths to feed, but Meyers is a viable flex option for Week 5, especially in deeper leagues. The Eagles are giving up 164 yards and one receiving touchdown per game to WRs, and they could be without top CB Quinyon Mitchell (knee) in Week 5, which would make things easier for some combination of Meyers, Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, and Josh Cameron.

free_agents.name: Bo Nix
free_agents.outlook: Bo Nix wasn't able to pull off another comeback win for the Broncos in a Week 4 loss to the 49ers. The third-year QB failed to complete 60% of his passes for a second straight game, and through four weeks, he's produced just six touchdowns (five passing, one rushing) while committing four turnovers. Denver's lack of a consistent running game isn't helping the offense find a rhythm, but Nix shoulders plenty of responsibility for the team's 2-2 start to the season. He'll try to bounce back in a Week 5 road game against a Chargers defense that's tied for 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to quarterbacks.

free_agents.name: Will Reichard
free_agents.outlook: Will Reichard should be a high-volume option once again as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Reichard stayed busy in Week 4 against the Dolphins, scoring all 15 of Minnesota's points from field goals. The third-year boot has now made three or more field goals in each of his last three games, and he's yet to miss a kick this year. He'll face a Saints squad that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against kickers this season,

free_agents.name: Alvin Kamara
free_agents.outlook: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain the Saints' top running back while Travis Etienne (hamstring) is sidelined during the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. In his first game without Etienne this season, Kamara totaled 58 yards on 12 touches, but his workload was largely impacted by the game script. He led New Orleans' backfield in targets (seven), which is a positive sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. Even so, Kamara is in for a tough Week 5 matchup against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 14.7 fantasy points per game to running backs this season, the fewest in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Devaughn Vele
free_agents.outlook: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain very involved in the Saints' offensive game plan in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Vele has been targeted 30 times (second-most on the team) through New Orleans' first four contests this season, logging 226 receiving yards and a pair of touchdowns. With Tyler Shough averaging a whopping 45 pass attempts per game this season, Vele will likely remain a solid fantasy option as the year progresses, at least until the return of Jordyn Tyson (hamstring, IR). However, Vele is in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 7.7 yards per target to opposing WRs this season.

free_agents.name: Blake Corum
free_agents.outlook: Blake Corum will aim to rebound from a pair of quiet games when the Rams host the Bills in Week 5. After after averaging 66.5 rushing yards in Los Angeles' first two games, Corum has totaled just 29 yards on the ground over his past two contests. He's been quite inefficient with his carries, logging just 2.6 yards per carry on his 11 totes while Kyren Williams has dominated backfield touches. Buffalo has given up six TDs to running backs this season, but three have come through the air. That's not Corum's forte -- he has just four catches for 20 yards with no scores as a receiver through four weeks.

free_agents.name: Kenny Gainwell
free_agents.outlook: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Gainwell found the end zone for the first time this season during the Week 4 loss to the Packers. However, he remains firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield, as Irving out-touched Gainwell 16 to five. Gainwell will likely struggle maintaining fantasy relevance in Week 5 without scoring another touchdown, though the Cowboys defense has already allowed four rushing TDs this season.

free_agents.name: Tyler Loop
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Loop and the Ravens pay a visit to the surging Falcons for a Week 5 interconference clash on Sunday Night Football. The second-year kicker went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and connected on all three PATs during Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4. Loop missed his second field goal of the season but set a new career high with his make from 64 yards out, and he's now 6-for-8 on field goals and a perfect 14-for-14 on extra points. Atlanta has scored the most points in the league over its last two games (80), meaning Loop and the Ravens will have to keep up in a potential high-scoring game.

free_agents.name: Spencer Shrader
free_agents.outlook: Spencer Shrader has made all seven of his field-goal attempts over the Colts' last two games and all 11 attempts this season. He has been one of the hottest waiver-wire options at kicker over the past couple of weeks and could be worth picking up if he's still available ahead of a Week 5 trip to Pittsburgh. The Steelers have allowed eight made field goals in four games and 21.8 points per game. Those who streamed Shrader against Washington in Week 4 may as well keep rolling with him in Week 5.

free_agents.name: Kenyon Sadiq
free_agents.outlook: Kenyon Sadiq faces an unsettled role in the Jets' limited passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Browns. After a Week 3 breakthrough performance, Sadiq failed to record a catch on four targets in Week 4 and now has 21 or fewer yards in three of his first four games. The Browns haven't allowed an opposing tight end to top 51 yards while surrendering just 6.7 yards per target, not boding well for Sadiq in Week 5. A potential Mason Taylor return would further dampen Sadiq's potential.

free_agents.name: Sam Darnold
free_agents.outlook: Sam Darnold will look to lead Seattle to victory in a key NFC West clash versus San Francisco in Week 5. Darnold threw for a modest 168 yards and was picked off once against the Chargers in Week 4, but he tossed two touchdowns and guided his team to a win. After playing only five snaps over the first two weeks due to a glute injury, Darnold looks to be back to full health and has posted a 6:3 TD:INT over the Seahawks' past two games. He could face a stiff challenge against the 49ers, who have yielded only three passing TDs through four weeks.

free_agents.name: Jordan Love
free_agents.outlook: Jordan Love will look to deliver a big win for the Packers in Week 5 against the Bears. Love completed 22 of 30 passes for 197 yards with a 2:1 TD:INT in a close win over Tampa Bay in Week 4. The veteran quarterback has now completed a career-low 56 percent of passes for 1,041 yards with eight touchdowns and three interceptions this season, with 300 or more passing yards in two of four outings. Love will take on a Chicago defense that's ranked 12th in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks this season.

free_agents.name: Evan McPherson
free_agents.outlook: Evan McPherson and the Bengals visit the Dolphins for a Week 5 road tilt. He made his only field-goal attempt from 29 yards out and connected on both of his PATs during Cincinnati's 22-17 loss in Week 4. McPherson remained perfect on his kicks through four outings, but he'll hope to get more involved against a Miami defense that ranks 21st in the league, allowing 25.3 points per game.

free_agents.name: Brian Robinson Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Brian Robinson is expected to remain involved in Atlanta's offensive game plan in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Robinson had his best game of the season in the Week 4 win over the Saints, accumulating 67 yards on 15 touches while scoring three touchdowns. The Alabama product has now logged double-digit carries in three straight games, suggesting that he's established himself as a valuable portion of this Falcons offense. Expect Robinson to remain Atlanta's No. 2 running back behind Bijan Robinson in a tougher Week 5 matchup against a Baltimore defense that's given up just 3.8 yards per carry to RBs this year.

free_agents.name: Dontayvion Wicks
free_agents.outlook: Dontayvion Wicks was expected to operate as the No. 1 wideout for the Eagles last game due to the injury to DeVonta Smith. Unfortunately, Philadelphia's offense was stymied, and Wicks managed three catches for just 18 yards in the 24-20 loss to the Rams. Smith appears unlikely to play in Week 5 versus the Jags, so Wicks should continue to play a prominent role in the offense. However, it was Darius Cooper who scored twice last game, and rookie Makai Lemon outpaced Wicks in both targets as well as receiving yards. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 against the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Dalton Schultz
free_agents.outlook: Dalton Schultz has recorded just 39 yards in two games since his 140-yard outburst for the Texans in Week 2. He's back to working as a supporting piece in Houston's passing game now that Nico Collins has recovered from a hamstring injury. The 30-year-old TE's inconsistent workloads keep him from being a reliable fantasy starter, and Schultz will be tough to trust in Week 5 against a Titans defense that's holding his position to 27 receiving yards per game, fourth-fewest in the NFL.

free_agents.name: C.J. Stroud
free_agents.outlook: C.J. Stroud has some streaming appeal in single-QB formats for Week 5, when the Texans travel to Tennessee for a battle between 0-4 AFC South squads. He has thrown for at least 347 yards in two of Houston's four losses and has a 5:0 TD:INT. The Titans have been respectable against the pass, with only four touchdowns allowed through the air this season, but other teams were able to build leads and run effectively on Tennessee. The Texans are unlikely to find as much success on the ground, considering RBs David Montgomery and Woody Marks have combined to average 2.9 yards per carry this season. Stroud has been asked to throw the ball 38 times per game, and he's likely to remain busy in Week 5. The Texans got top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) back from a two-game absence in Week 4, and Collins contributed immediately in his return by catching both of Stroud's touchdown passes in a 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.

free_agents.name: Will Shipley
free_agents.outlook: Will Shipley may be the only healthy running back left for the Eagles. Tank Bigsby replaced an injured Saquon Barkley last game for the Eagles, only to suffer an injury of his own late in the contest. Bigsby rushed 14 times for 55 yards to lead the Eagles before exiting with a lower-body issue. His status is up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags, as is Barkley's due to a hamstring ailment. If neither Bigsby nor Barkley can play, Shipley would be in line for an expanded role. Shipley did have six rushes for 23 yards following the injury to Bigsby. However, Jacksonville has played the run extremely well thus far in 2026. The Jags are allowing just 74.3 rushing yards per tote, which us second in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Hunter Henry
free_agents.outlook: Hunter Henry could have an expanded role in Week 5 when the Patriots face the Raiders with Eli Raridon (ankle) uncertain. Henry was already playing at least 70% of the snaps, and he posted a season-high five catches for 62 yards in Week 4, collecting five targets for the second time this season. Las Vegas has allowed five touchdown catches to opposing tight ends, but also just 6.1 yards per target through four games, suggesting Henry may need to find the end zone for the first time in 2026 to be a fantasy asset.

free_agents.name: Kalif Raymond
free_agents.outlook: Kalif Raymond will seek to reestablish himself as a consistent option in Chicago's passing game against the Packers in Week 5. After totaling 19 catches for 214 yards and one touchdown across the Bears' first three games of the season, Raymond recorded just two catches for six yards versus the Jets in Week 4 with Tyson Bagent under center. The veteran pass catcher will have Bagent throwing to him once again this Sunday, but he will also face a Green Bay defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against wide receivers so far this campaign.

free_agents.name: Tyler Allgeier
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Allgeier may be lined up for a big role for Arizona in Week 5 against the Lions. Rookie Jeremiyah Love is dealing with an ankle injury, and if he can't suit up Sunday, Allgeier will likely lead the team's backfield. Even with Love healthy for nearly the entire game in Week 4, Allgeier posted good production, recording an 8-42-1 rushing line and two catches for seven yards. The Cardinals' RB group could find success against a Lions defense that is giving up 4.64 yards per carry to running backs, eighth-worst in the league.

free_agents.name: Tyjae Spears
free_agents.outlook: Tyjae Spears has been limited to three touches in each of Tennessee's Week 3 and Week 4 games while playing through an ankle injury. Typically, his total is in the high single digits, but Spears' injury concerns, coupled with Tennessee's struggles on offense (13.8 points per game), make the change-of-pace RB a fantasy non-factor ahead of a Week 5 home game against the Texans, who are allowing just 3.5 yards per carry. Tony Pollard should continue to get the majority of opportunities in Tennessee's backfield.

free_agents.name: Malik Washington
free_agents.outlook: Malik Washington's volume continues to be steady for the Dolphins as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals. He hauled in five of QB Malik WIllis' nine completions in Week 4, his fourth-straight week with at least five targets while increasing his yardage in each of the last three outings. Cincinnati's secondary hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 63 yards, and while Washington's workload shouldn't be questioned, his potential remains capped by Miami's low-scoring offense.

free_agents.name: Kirk Cousins
free_agents.outlook: Kirk Cousins went down swinging in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, setting season highs with 52 pass attempts and 365 yards while throwing multiple TDs for a fourth straight game to begin the season. While rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza waits in the wings, Cousins' 11 touchdowns are tied for the league lead, and he sits just outside the top 10 in passing yards and completion rate, which should give him plenty of job security. The veteran quarterback will try to keep rolling in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that is tied for ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to the position.

free_agents.name: Keon Coleman
free_agents.outlook: Keon Coleman's role in the Bills offense remains unsettled ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. DJ Moore exited Week 4 after aggravating a shoulder injury that forced a similar result in Week 2, and Coleman again shined. In the two games with Moore leaving early, Coleman has 12 catches on 13 targets for 179 yards and a touchdown. With Moore playing four quarters, Coleman has two catches for 38 yards. Facing a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 50 yards leaves Coleman as a fantasy risk regardless of Moore's status.

free_agents.name: Rashid Shaheed
free_agents.outlook: Rashid Shaheed should continue to operate in a versatile role for Seattle in a big Week 5 battle against San Francisco. Though Shaheed had just one catch for 20 yards versus the Chargers in Week 4, he added two carries for 33 yards and a touchdown while also returning kickoffs and punts. The 49ers have a similarly versatile player in Deebo Samuel, and the pair of Swiss-army-knife wideouts could be keys in what figures to be a battle of tough defenses. San Francisco has allowed just 17.0 fantasy points per game to WRs this season, sixth-best in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Tre Tucker
free_agents.outlook: Tre Tucker handled a season-high eight targets in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, but he turned them into just four catches for 44 yards. The fourth-year wideout has reached 50 receiving yards only once in four games to begin the season, producing a 15-233-1 line on 23 targets. With a healthy Brock Bowers back as Kirk Cousins' No. 1 option, Tucker's chances of another ceiling game have shrunk. He'll face a Patriots secondary in Week 5 that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and could be without top cornerback Christian Gonzalez.

free_agents.name: Jayden Reed
free_agents.outlook: Jayden Reed will not play in Week 5 as the Packers play the Bears. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, and he'll now require season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Skyy Moore and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.

free_agents.name: Tank Dell
free_agents.outlook: Tank Dell (knee) is expected to have his practice window opened ahead of the Texans' Week 5 road game against the Titans. The 2023 third-round pick hasn't played since sustaining a significant knee injury in Week 16 of the 2024 season. Dell is currently on injured reserve and will likely take some time to ramp up. He's unlikely to return in Week 5 against Tennessee, but forward-looking fantasy managers should take notice of Dell's impending return, as he averaged 55 receiving yards and scored 10 TDs in 25 games prior to his injury.

free_agents.name: Cairo Santos
free_agents.outlook: Cairo Santos will look to deliver on high volume again as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Bagent converted a season-high three field goals against the Jets in Week 3, and he also nailed both of his XPAs. The veteran kicker has now gone 7-for-8 on field-goal attempts while making all 13 of his extra-point tries across four weeks this season. He'll face a Green Bay defense that's ranked top five against fantasy kickers so far.

free_agents.name: Kaelon Black
free_agents.outlook: Kaelon Black should continue to back up 49ers star RB Christian McCaffrey in Week 5 against Seattle. Black surprisingly logged 14 carries in Week 1 against the Rams, but since then he's topped out at seven totes as McCaffrey has dominated touches out of the backfield. Black also has just one catch this season, so he hasn't been able to establish much fantasy value except as an insurance policy in case of a McCaffrey injury. It may be hard for Black to find success on what will likely be limited opportunities against Seattle, as the Seahawks are allowing a paltry 3.35 yards per carry to RBs this season.

free_agents.name: Chris Boswell
free_agents.outlook: Chris Boswell and the Steelers return home to take on the Colts in Week 5. He finished Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4 converting one of two field-goal attempts while connecting on his lone extra-point try. Boswell's miss came from 48 yards out, and he's now 1-for-4 on kicks equal to or longer than that across four games in 2026. He'll aim to bounce back versus an Indianapolis defense giving up 26.0 points per contest, which ranks 21st in the league.

free_agents.name: Brenton Strange
free_agents.outlook: Brenton Strange became the latest TE to take advantage of a Bengals defense that has allowed the most yards in the league to the position. He compiled 95 receiving yards in Week 4 against Cincinnati to lead the Jaguars. Strange had recorded just 72 yards over the preceding three games combined, and he's likely to return to a reduced role in Week 5 against an Eagles defense that's holding TEs to 39 yards per game and has yet to allow a TD to the position. While Strange can be worth streaming in the right matchups, Week 5 isn't one of those.

free_agents.name: Roman Wilson
free_agents.outlook: Roman Wilson and the Steelers take on the Colts at home in Week 5. He caught three of six targets for 74 yards and one touchdown during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss. Wilson tied for second on the team in receptions and targets while finishing second in yardage, and he now has a TD catch in two consecutive contests. He's been a reliable option for Aaron Rodgers, as he's generated six targets in all four outings this season en route to a 14-188-2 line. Wilson's next opportunity comes against the Colts' 20th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (35.0) to WRs.

free_agents.name: Keaton Mitchell
free_agents.outlook: Keaton Mitchell's role in the Chargers' backfield continues to grow. The former Raven handled a season-high 15 touches in a Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, turning them into 63 scrimmage yards, while Omarion Hampton produced 53 yards and a rushing TD on 11 touches, and Kimani Vidal added 36 yards and a receiving score on seven touches. That split points toward offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel moving into a full-blown backfield committee, and while Mitchell's volume has been trending up, he hasn't done much yet to make a case for the No. 1 spot on the depth chart. He'll look to make his own trip to the end zone in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Mike Gesicki
free_agents.outlook: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals travel to take on the winless Dolphins in Week 5. He grabbed three of five targets for 40 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's Week 4 loss. Gesicki now has two straight outings with a TD and recorded his third overall, and he could be in line for an uptick in opportunities in a favorable matchup versus a Miami defense that allows 18.6 fantasy points to TEs, which is tied for 28th. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion), Tee Higgins (adductor), and Colbie Young (knee) are all questionable, potentially leaving Gesicki as one of Joe Burrow's primary receivers against a Dolphins unit that just gave up 13 receptions and 119 yards to T.J. Hockenson

free_agents.name: Adonai Mitchell
free_agents.outlook: Adonai Mitchell needs to overcome a finger injury that has cost him the last two weeks if he's to help the Jets against the Browns in Week 5. Prior to injury, Mitchell was giving the Jets a field-stretching option, averaging 13.7 yards per catch on nine grabs. Targets will continue to be heavily funneled toward Garrett Wilson, but Mitchell will be in a favorable spot if cleared to play, as Cleveland has allowed six touchdowns to opposing receivers through four games. Sterling Shepard and Isaiah Williams would continue to register additional snaps should Mitchell miss his third straight game.

free_agents.name: Isiah Pacheco
free_agents.outlook: Isiah Pacheco will remain out in Week 5 when Detroit travels to Arizona. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return this season in jeopardy. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will continue to handle RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.

free_agents.name: Pat Freiermuth
free_agents.outlook: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers welcome the Colts to town for a Week 5 home tilt. He played 75% of snaps on offense and caught three of five targets for 17 yards and his second touchdown of the season. Fellow tight end Darnell Washington (3-27-1) was slightly more productive while playing 70% of the offensive snaps during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. They're both listed as starting tight ends for the Steelers, and it looks like it'll be a toss-up between the two on any given week as long as they're healthy. Indianapolis allows 13.7 fantasy points per game to TEs, which ranks 17th.

free_agents.name: Daniel Jones
free_agents.outlook: Daniel Jones is averaging 189 passing yards per game heading into the Colts' Week 5 trip to Pittsburgh. Jones threw for a season-high 342 yards against the Steelers last season but had five turnovers in that game. His passing production is likely to be much more muted in this rematch while throwing to a depleted Colts receiving corps that remains without Alec Pierce (heel; IR) and played without Keenan Allen (groin) in the Week 4 win over the Commanders in London. Pittsburgh's defense has limited QBs to a 5:4 TD:INT, while Jones has an even worse 3:4 TD:INT this season. Even superflex and multi-QB league managers are better off looking elsewhere.

free_agents.name: Mike Washington Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Mike Washington failed to produce another big play in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, managing only 18 rushing yards on nine carries while catching one of two targets for minus-1 yard. Ashton Jeanty continues to struggle on the ground, but Washington hasn't yet shown enough consistency to be any kind of threat to his workload on early downs. The rookie is averaging 5.0 yards on his first 24 NFL carries, though, well clear of Jeanty's 3.4 mark, so volume could begin to tilt his way a little more if that trend continues. Washington will try to break free in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that ranked 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Rashod Bateman
free_agents.outlook: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens square off against the 2-2 Falcons on the road in Week 5. He caught both of his targets for 46 yards during Baltimore's 24-18 victory in Week 4. Bateman tied with five other Ravens in targets while finishing second on the team in yardage, but Zay Flowers (8-118-1) and Mark Andrews (5-27-1) did most of the damage on offense. He'll try to make more of a contribution versus an Atlanta defense that's tied for 27th in fantasy points allowed (38.4) per game to WRs, although that could be challenging given Lamar Jackson's (ankle) uncertain status for Week 5.

free_agents.name: Deshaun Watson
free_agents.outlook: Deshaun Watson and the Browns take their surprising 3-1 record into a road battle against the Jets in Week 5. In Week 4's 27-24 victory, he threw for 268 yards (24-for-33) with one TD and one INT, while rushing seven times for 22 yards. Watson lost one of his two fumbles, but he was able to do enough to lead his team to a third straight win. He hit seven different receivers en route to his highest passing yardage total since 2023. Watson aims to keep improving in a tough matchup versus the Jets, who have the second-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (16.0) to QBs.

free_agents.name: Aaron Rodgers
free_agents.outlook: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers host the Colts for a Week 5 showdown. He threw for 299 yards (22-for-40) with three TDs and two INTs during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. That's two straight outings with three passing TDs and nearly 300 yards through the air, but the 42-year-old was sacked five times in addition to his two turnovers. Rodgers will look to clean up the mistakes against a Colts defense allowing 24.3 fantasy points per game to QBs (27th) and 261.3 passing yards (29th).

free_agents.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Chris Rodriguez has a consistent role as the Jaguars' No. 2 RB behind Bhayshul Tuten, but Rodriguez's usage level is too low to warrant lineup consideration in most formats. Rodriguez has recorded between six and eight carries in each of his first four games with the Jaguars. He's riding a two-game TD streak but has been a complete non-factor in the passing game with zero targets while averaging a mediocre 4.2 yards per carry. Jacksonville faces an Eagles defense in Week 5 that ranks among the 10 most generous to RBs on the ground, allowing 106 rushing yards per game to the position.

free_agents.name: Jaylen Wright
free_agents.outlook: Jaylen Wright hasn't emerged from the Dolphins' backfield ahead of a Week 5 tilt against the Bengals. After missing Week 3, Wright was thought to have an ascending role following De'Von Achane's season-ending knee injury but received only five carries in Week 4 while Ollie Gordon shined with 100 yards and a touchdown on nine carries. It doesn't appear Wright was limited by the foot issue that cost him a game, as he remained the team's primary kick returner. Facing a defense that's allowing 4.5 yards per carry should afford Wright additional running lanes, but the role uncertainty puts Wright in wait-and-see territory rather than as a viable flex option.

free_agents.name: Caleb Douglas
free_agents.outlook: Caleb Douglas will need to overcome an ankle injury to help the Dolphins against the Bengals in Week 5. He missed the last two weeks, and his role in this low-volume passing offense is questionable; he drew seven targets in Week 1 and only three in Week 2. The Bengals defense is much improved and ranks 14th in points allowed to opposing wideouts, with no receiver topping 63 yards against them. While Douglas can stretch the field, availability and usage remain question marks.

free_agents.name: Trey Smack
free_agents.outlook: Trey Smack will look to be consistent for the Packers once again in Week 5 against the Bears. Smack nailed a 58-yard field goal and both of his extra-point tries against the Buccaneers in Week 4. The rookie kicker has now gone 6-for-7 on field-goal kicks this season, with three of them from 50-plus yards. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked top five against fantasy kickers this campaign.

free_agents.name: Jerry Jeudy
free_agents.outlook: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns travel to take on the Jets in Week 5. He hauled in all three of his targets for 36 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 4, setting new season highs in receptions and yardage. Jeudy had a solid bounce-back effort after failing to record a target in Week 3, but he remains behind Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion, and Harold Fannin Jr. in the offensive pecking order. Jeudy belongs on fantasy benches against a Jets defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points allowed (28.5) per game to WRs.

free_agents.name: Kendre Miller
free_agents.outlook: Kendre Miller is likely to remain one of the Saints' top rushers while Travis Etienne (hamstring) is out during the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Miller received the second-most carries (six) on New Orleans in the Week 4 loss to the Falcons but was largely ineffective, averaging just 1.5 yards per carry. Even if Miller continues splitting work with Alvin Kamara, he likely won't have much fantasy value, as the Saints' offense is averaging a whopping 45 pass attempts per game. Additionally, Miller is in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Vikings defense that's allowed just 307 rushing yards all season.

free_agents.name: Dohnte Meyers
free_agents.outlook: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals travel to take on the 0-4 Dolphins in Week 5. He caught seven of nine targets for 82 yards during Cincinnati's 22-17 Week 4 loss, setting new career highs across his receiving line, while returning six kickoffs for 161 yards and two punts for nine yards. Meyers finished second on the team in receiving yards and third in receptions and targets, and there's a decent chance he could earn a similar workload versus Miami's third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (22.2) to WRs. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) are both questionable to play, along with fellow rookie Colbie Young (knee), and Andre Iosivas (thumb, IR) remains out for Week 5.

free_agents.name: Cooper Kupp
free_agents.outlook: Cooper Kupp will look to rebound from a quiet performance when Seattle faces San Francisco in Week 5. Against the Chargers this past Sunday, Kupp caught just one of two targets for 13 yards. It was his lowest offensive output of the season, though he's been pretty quiet overall with two or fewer receptions in three of four contests so far. The 49ers are yielding just 123.5 receiving yards per game to wideouts, seventh-fewest in the league.

free_agents.name: George Holani
free_agents.outlook: George Holani looks to be locked in as Seattle's No. 2 RB heading into a Week 5 clash against the 49ers. That role didn't yield much fruit for Holani in Week 4, however, as he recorded just 18 yards on seven carries and two yards on one reception. Meanwhile, Emanuel Wilson recorded 120 total yards and two TDs on 24 touches, so he looks to be in full control of the backfield for the time being. San Francisco has given up just two touchdowns (one rushing, one receiving) to running backs this season, so they aren't a great draw for a player like Holani who probably needs to get into the end zone to put up meaningful fantasy points.

free_agents.name: Tank Bigsby
free_agents.outlook: Tank Bigsby replaced an injured Saquon Barkley last game for the Eagles, only to suffer an injury of his own late in the contest. Bigsby rushed 14 times for 55 yards to lead the Eagles before exiting with a lower-body issue. His status is up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. If neither Bigsby nor Barkley can play, Will Shipley would be in line for an expanded role. However, Jacksonville has played the run extremely well thus far in 2026. The Jags are allowing just 74.3 rushing yards per tote, which us second in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Justice Hill
free_agents.outlook: Justice Hill and the Ravens visit the Falcons for a Week 5 showdown. He rushed once for three yards and caught two of three targets for 22 yards during Baltimore's 24-18 victory in Week 4. Derrick Henry out-carried Hill 23-1, even with Lamar Jackson missing the entire second half with an ankle injury. It appears that regardless of who's under center, the Ravens' backfield belongs to Henry. Hill should remain on fantasy benches against an Atlanta defense allowing just 17.9 points per game to RBs, which ranks ninth.

free_agents.name: Calvin Ridley
free_agents.outlook: Calvin Ridley has just three catches for 48 yards on five targets through four games. He's barely contributing as the No. 4 WR in a Titans offense that's averaging just 13.8 points per game, which is the second-fewest in the NFL. Even in a Week 5 matchup against a Texans defense that has struggled to defend wide receivers, Ridley remains a non-factor in fantasy.

free_agents.name: Mack Hollins
free_agents.outlook: Mack Hollins' availability for Week 5 against the Raiders is in doubt due to a calf injury. Hollins has been a steady but unspectacular piece for the Patriots' receiving corps, going for 51 or more yards three times despite topping five targets just once with A.J. Brown sidelined by an ankle injury. Las Vegas can be vulnerable to opposing receivers, surrendering 70 or more yards four times. Efton Chism filled in after Hollins' early Week 4 exit and would likely do so again if Hollins does not suit up.

free_agents.name: Malik Willis
free_agents.outlook: Malik Willis will seek a breakthrough outing in Week 5 when the Dolphins face the Bengals. He has accounted for just two total touchdowns through four games and completed a mere nine passes for 85 yards in Week 4, both season-lows. An improved Cincinnati defense has allowed only four touchdown passes, but all of them have come over the last two weeks. With Miami's defense likely to give up points, Willis will at least have the opportunity to produce at a higher level than he's shown thus far.

free_agents.name: Tyler Bass
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Bass remains a stable floor, low ceiling kicking option for the Bills as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. Bass has collected 14 extra points through four weeks as Buffalo routinely converts drives into touchdowns, but only six field goal attempts, where he's perfect, keeping his scoring capacity limited. The Rams' defense has been stingy to opposing kickers, so don't expect Week 5 to be Bass' breakout party.

free_agents.name: Michael Penix Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Michael Penix will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Penix has been great through two starts in 2026, throwing for 479 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. He's helped rejuvenate Atlanta's offense, as the team has scored a whopping 40 points per game since his return. Despite this, Penix is in for a tougher Week 5 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed just 18.8 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season.

free_agents.name: Darius Cooper
free_agents.outlook: Darius Cooper scored twice last game for the Eagles. Cooper finished the contests with seven targets, parlaying those looks into three catches for 33 yards and the pair of scores. If Devonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and/or Saquon Barkley are sidelined in Week 5 versus the Jags, Cooper could see an uptick in usage again.  Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Geno Smith
free_agents.outlook: Geno Smith hopes for more opportunities in the Jets' Week 5 game against a vulnerable Browns secondary. After completing 31 passes in Week 3, Smith went just 8-for-15 in Week 4 against the Bears. Despite the lack of volume, he has a 5:0 TD:INT ratio and a 7.7 yards-per-attempt average, his highest mark since playing just two games in 2016. Cleveland has allowed nine touchdown passes in four games and at least 291 yards in each of the last two weeks, putting Smith in a spot to exceed his season norms.

free_agents.name: Malachi Fields
free_agents.outlook: Malachi Fields scored his first NFL touchdown last game for the Giants. The rookie flashed his big-play ability, snagging a 40-yarder from quarterback Jameis Winston along with the 12-yard score. He finished with two catches for a career-best 52 yards and the touchdown. In Week 5, Fields and company will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass. Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.

free_agents.name: Matt Gay
free_agents.outlook: Matt Gay continues to benefit from the Raiders' surprisingly strong start to the season on offense with Kirk Cousins under center. In a Week 4 loss to Kansas City, Gay was a perfect 4-for-4 on FG tries while also converting his only PAT. The veteran has yet to miss an attempt in 2026, going 10-for-10 on FGs and 9-for-9 on extra points, putting him third in the NFL in kicker scoring behind the Vikings' Will Reichard and the Colts' Spencer Shrader. Gay likely won't be able to afford to start squandering opportunities in Week 5 against a Patriots team that's allowed 19.3 points per game so far, tied for sixth in the league.

free_agents.name: Najee Harris
free_agents.outlook: Najee Harris has received nine carries in each of the last two games for the Giants. However, he is averaging just 4.0 yards per carry as teams dare the Giants to throw with backup quarterback Jameis Winston, and remains behind Cam Skattebo on the depth chart. In Week 5, the G-Men will face a rather stingy Washington run defense. The Commanders are allowing just 93.5 yards per tilt on the ground, which is sixth in the league. However, Washington did allow three rushing touchdowns last game versus the Colts.

free_agents.name: Kayshon Boutte
free_agents.outlook: Kayshon Boutte is averaging 29 receiving yards per game and has yet to score this season for the Texans. The former Patriots wide receiver hasn't shown enough with his new team to warrant lineup consideration in most fantasy formats in Week 5 against a Titans defense that has allowed three TDs to WRs through four games. Three other Texans wideouts have more yards than Boutte this season, as does TE Dalton Schultz.

free_agents.name: AJ Barner
free_agents.outlook: AJ Barner will look to amp up his production for Seattle in a Week 5 clash against the 49ers. Barner caught just one of three targets for 12 yards against the Chargers this past Sunday after posting a promising 5-69-0 receiving line the previous week. Barner logged nine targets in that Week 3 win over Washington, but he's drawn three or fewer targets in each of his other three contests. San Francisco has been tough against tight ends this season, giving up just 4.0 points per game to the position (fifth-best in the NFL).

free_agents.name: Samaje Perine
free_agents.outlook: Samaje Perine and the Bengals are on the road to take on the Dolphins in Week 5. He tallied three carries for seven yards and failed to bring in his only target during Cincinnati's Week 4 defeat. Perine's offensive snaps and involvement continue to fluctuate as the clear back behind Chase Brown, even despite his team playing from behind more recently. Miami's defense ranks last in fantasy points (29.7) allowed to RBs, but Perine should remain on fantasy benches.

free_agents.name: Jake Elliott
free_agents.outlook: Jake Elliott still managed two field goals and two extra points last game for Philadelphia, despite massive struggles on offense for the Eagles. Elliott has just four field goals through four contests, as the Philadelphia offense has sputtered in part due to a bevy of injuries to skill players. With DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and potentially Saquon Barkley sidelined for Week 5 versus the Jags, points may be at a premium. The Jags have also been extremely stingy in terms of points allowed this season. Jacksonville is giving up only 13.3 points per tilt, which is second in the league.

free_agents.name: Chad Ryland
free_agents.outlook: Chad Ryland showed off his leg in Week 4 and will look to do so again when the Cardinals square off against the Lions in Week 5. Though Ryland had only one field-goal attempt against the Giants this past Sunday, he impressed with a 60-yarder just before halftime. Ryland has now made eight of nine field-goal tries this season while nailing all nine of his point-after attempts. He could get plenty of opportunities against the Lions, who have given up a league-worst 31.8 points per game through four weeks.

free_agents.name: Chris Brooks
free_agents.outlook: Chris Brooks will remain an option in Green Bay's crowded backfield if he's healthy in Week 5 against the Bears. Brooks rushed a solid four times for 30 yards and caught one ball for five yards in the first quarter of Week 4, but he then injured his ankle and did not record a stat after. The fourth-year running back will need to log some healthy practices this week if he hopes to play against the Packers' big rival. If he's able to suit up, Brooks will face a Bears defense that's allowed bottom-10 (4.73) yards per carry for RBs this season.

free_agents.name: Antonio Williams
free_agents.outlook: Antonio Williams had eight targets last game for Washington, which was second on the squad behind Stefon Diggs. Unfortunately, Williams could muster just three catches for 21 yards in the lackluster loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, which would certainly be a boost for Williams, regardless of whether Terry McLaurin also suits up. McLaurin was sidelined with a hamstring issue. New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, though, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Tre' Harris
free_agents.outlook: Tre' Harris is still looking for his first touchdown of the season, but he's been Justin Herbert's most reliable option, topping 50 receiving yards in each of the Chargers' last three games. Harris has put together a 13-209-0 line on 21 targets over four weeks, and he could make a push for the top spot on the WR depth chart with Ladd McConkey now dealing with both rib and foot injuries and Quentin Johnston failing to do much with his opportunities. Harris will aim for his first trip to the end zone in 2026 in Week 5 against a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs, but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain.

free_agents.name: Cam Ward
free_agents.outlook: Cam Ward hasn't thrown multiple touchdown passes in a game during the Titans' 0-4 start, and he's just 3-18 as a starter with 18 touchdown passes in 21 games. The 2025 first overall pick isn't an advisable fantasy option in Week 5 against the Texans, who have surprisingly surrendered the third-most passing yards in the league this season but still boast plenty of talent on defense and allowed the sixth-fewest passing yards in 2025. Dynasty managers looking for a silver lining with Ward can point to his season-high 222 passing yards in the Week 4 loss to Baltimore, 145 of which went to rookie fourth overall pick Carnell Tate.

free_agents.name: Jalen Nailor
free_agents.outlook: Jalen Nailor's tough start to his Raiders tenure continued in Week 4, as he failed to get a target before leaving the game early due to a concussion. The former Viking has a meager 5-52-0 line on just 11 targets through four weeks, and while his spot in the lineup seems secure when he's healthy due to his blocking ability, he hasn't established much chemistry with Kirk Cousins despite the fact that the duo played together in Minnesota. If Nailor does clear the concussion protocol in time, he'll be little more than a dart throw in Week 5, even against a Patriots secondary that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and which could be without top cornerback Christian Gonzalez.

free_agents.name: Jauan Jennings
free_agents.outlook: Jauan Jennings remains a secondary option in the passing game ahead of Minnesota's Week 5 matchup at New Orleans. Jennings was projected to benefit from Justin Jefferson sitting out Week 4 with an ankle injury, but the veteran wideout logged just one catch for eight yards. He's now recorded two catches for nine yards in two weeks mostly without Jefferson, which especially doesn't bode well for his value when the star pass catcher returns to the field. He'll face a Saints defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this season.

free_agents.name: Oronde Gadsden
free_agents.outlook: Oronde Gadsden garnered his first significant target volume of the season in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, catching five of eight targets for 36 yards. The second-year tight end doesn't have the blocking chops offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel prefers, but with Charlie Kolar and David Njoku both injured and the team's wide receiver room also banged up, Gadsden is one of Justin Herbert's best remaining pass catchers. He'll try to build on this performance in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in receiving yards allowed to TEs through four weeks.

free_agents.name: Kaleb Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Kaleb Johnson will seek to stay involved as the Packers take on the Bears in Week 5. Johnson finished Week 4 against the Buccaneers with a solid eight carries for 42 yards, but he also lost a critical fumble in the fourth quarter. This makes it unclear what the backfield split will look like moving forward, not that there's been much of a clear breakdown so far. Chicago has ranked 26th in yards per carry allowed to RBs this season, which could carve a path for Johnson to stay productive if he can hold onto the ball.

free_agents.name: Ray Davis
free_agents.outlook: Ray Davis has not been a part of the Bills' game plan entering a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. He has only two carries through four weeks, adding one catch while factoring in on kickoff returns. Seemingly losing snaps to Ty Johnson on passing downs in what was already a limited role, Davis's only fantasy appeal would be to James Cook managers in the event of an injury.

free_agents.name: Nick Folk
free_agents.outlook: Nick Folk is expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Falcons' Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Since the return of Michael Penix in Week 3, Folk has converted all 12 of his kicks (three field goals and nine extra points), averaging 9.0 kicking points per game. With Atlanta's recent offensive success (40.0 points per game over the last two weeks) and Baltimore's defense having allowed 24.0 points and 7.5 kicking points per game, Folk is expected to have a favorable Week 5 matchup.

free_agents.name: Jaylin Noel
free_agents.outlook: Jaylin Noel turned three targets into 85 yards for the Texans in their Week 4 loss to Dallas, and the 2025 third-round pick continues to make the most of his opportunities. Heading into a Week 5 road game against the Titans, Noel has caught eight of 12 targets for 186 yards while leading the league with 23.3 yards per reception. Noel's big-play potential makes him worth a flier in deeper formats against a Titans secondary that has been prone to breakdowns, but he hasn't garnered consistent enough volume from C.J. Stroud to be started comfortably in any matchup.

free_agents.name: Isaiah Davis
free_agents.outlook: Isaiah Davis hasn't factored into the Jets' offensive plans ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Browns. Despite Breece Hall's (quad) Week 4 absence, Davis didn't receive a rushing opportunity and has no official offensive touches to date. Braelon Allen would again lead the Jets' backfield should Hall sit out again in Week 5.

free_agents.name: Ryan Flournoy
free_agents.outlook: Ryan Flournoy has been targeted at least four times in every game this season for the Cowboys. However, he has yet to cross 40 yards receiving in any contest. Versus the Texans, he had four catches but only for a season-high 37 yards. With a lot of mouths to feed like CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and even tight end Jake Ferguson, Flournoy's output may continue to be depressed. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league. Flournoy is still looking for his first score of the season.

free_agents.name: Wil Lutz
free_agents.outlook: Wil Lutz continues to get little volume thanks to the struggles of the Broncos' offense. Through four games, the veteran kicker has attempted only five extra points, converting all, while going just 5-for-7 on FG attempts, with one of his misses coming from 58 yards out. Lutz is reliable, especially with most of his games coming either at altitude or indoors, but without more opportunities, he won't be able to make much of a contribution. He could get more chances in Week 5 against a Chargers team that has allowed 26.5 points per game, 24th in the league.

free_agents.name: Xavier Hutchinson
free_agents.outlook: Xavier Hutchinson has exactly three catches in every game this season for the Texans and is averaging 42 receiving yards per game heading into a Week 5 road game against the Titans. He has drawn 11 targets in two games playing alongside Nico Collins and 15 targets during the two games Collins missed due to a hamstring injury. Collins should continue to work as C.J. Stroud's No. 1 option against Tennessee's beatable secondary, while the remainder of Houston's receiving corps is best left on the bench or waiver wire, Hutchinson included.

free_agents.name: Jameis Winston
free_agents.outlook: Jameis Winston tossed three touchdowns last game for the Giants. It was the full Jameis Winston experience, though, as the veteran also threw two interceptions. However, he finished 18-of-29 for 250 yards in the 36-24 win over the Cardinals. Miraculously, the G-Men currently sit in first place in the NFC East. In Week 5, Jameis and company will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass.  Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.

free_agents.name: Dominic Zvada
free_agents.outlook: Dominic Zvada continues to shine for the Giants as a rookie. Zvada made all three of his field goals, as well as an extra point, in the 36-24 win over the Cardinals. Two of Zvada's field goals were from 50-plus yards out. He is perfect to begin his NFL career, with five field goals already from 50-plus yards away. He could be primed for a big output in Week 5 versus a Commanders squad allowing 30.5 points per tilt, which is 31st in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Chris Bell
free_agents.outlook: Chris Bell is failing to gain traction in the Dolphins' limited passing attack ahead of a Week 5 tilt with the Bengals. Bell failed to record a catch on three targets in Week 4 in a game where Miami threw only 17 times, completing nine of them. Bell remains long on potential, but he's garnered three or fewer looks in three of Miami's first four games, and a breakout against a middling Bengals defense that hasn't allowed more than 63 yards to an opposing receiver seems unlikely.

free_agents.name: Cade Otton
free_agents.outlook: Cade Otton will operate as the Buccaneers' top tight end in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Otton led Tampa Bay in receiving yards during the Week 4 loss to the Packers, hauling in four of six targets for 37 yards. He appears to have a connection with rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels and could be a solid spot-start in Week 5, especially while facing a Dallas defense that's given up 15.3 fantasy points per game and three receiving touchdowns to opposing tight ends this season.

free_agents.name: Tyler Higbee
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Higbee may have worked his way back up to the Rams' No. 1 tight-end role with a Week 5 matchup against Buffalo on tap. After logging just two catches over the first two weeks of the season, Higbee has tallied a 13-129-1 line over the past two weeks. He's led Los Angeles tight ends in offensive snaps in each of those contests, with injuries to Colby Parkinson (shoulder) and Terrance Ferguson (ankle - IR) contributing to the uptick in playing time. Buffalo has given up just one touchdown to tight ends so far this season.

free_agents.name: Daniel Carlson
free_agents.outlook: Daniel Carlson could get few scoring chances in the Saints' Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Carlson missed another field goal in the Week 4 loss to the Falcons and is now just one of three on tries from 50-or-more yards. On the season, he's converted five of seven field-goal tries and 10 of 11 point-after attempts. Carlson likely won't have many scoring opportunities in the Week 5 matchup as well, with Minnesota's defense allowing just 12.8 points and 6.8 kicking points per game.

free_agents.name: Chig Okonkwo
free_agents.outlook: Chig Okonkwo returned to the lineup for the Commanders following a two-game absence due to a hamstring ailment. Okonkwo was targeted four times, but managed two catches for a mere five yards in the dismal 30-13 loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, though, which would certainly be a boost for the passing game. However, New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Isaac TeSlaa
free_agents.outlook: Isaac TeSlaa could continue to have a big role as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. TeSlaa finished Week 4 against the Panthers with season-high targets, catches and yards, reeling in four of eight looks for four catches and 95 yards. After a slow start to the season, the second-year pass catcher has now posted a 7-161-0 receiving line in the last two games. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to the wide receiver position.

free_agents.name: Evan Engram
free_agents.outlook: Evan Engram tied his season high with five targets in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers, but the additional volume didn't lead to much production as he caught only one of them for six yards. Over the last three games, the veteran tight end has a meager 2-23-0 line on eight targets, remaining an afterthought in the offense. No. 3 wide receiver Pat Bryant left the loss to San Francisco with an ankle sprain, which could result in more volume for Engram, but that may not be enough to make him relevant again. Engram will try to take advantage of his opportunities in Week 5 against a Chargers defense that's tied for 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

free_agents.name: Gunnar Helm
free_agents.outlook: Gunnar Helm is averaging just 15 receiving yards per game heading into Tennessee's Week 5 home game against the Texans. The second-year TE has exceeded 70% of offensive snaps in every game this season, but Helm is being used more as a blocker than a pass catcher in Tennessee's struggling offense. Houston is allowing 56 yards per game to TEs but hasn't given up a TD to the position, while Helm has scored just twice in 20 career NFL games. Helm hasn't done enough to warrant fantasy consideration.

free_agents.name: Germie Bernard
free_agents.outlook: Germie Bernard and the Steelers return home to square off against the Colts in Week 5. The rookie wideout caught both of his targets for 11 yards during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. Bernard should remain on fantasy benches while playing behind veterans DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman, and Jaylen Warren, along with tight ends Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington. Indianapolis allows 35.0 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 20th, but his limited involvement on offense doesn't inspire much confidence.

free_agents.name: Tyson Bagent
free_agents.outlook: Tyson Bagent is primed to get the starting nod once again as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Bagent completed 25 of 34 passes for 268 yards and an interception in a win over the Jets during Week 4, which was enough for Ben Johnson to announce him as the starter once again. The D2 product will now have to face a Packers defense on their home turf, which has ranked top ten against fantasy quarterbacks this season.

free_agents.name: Pat Bryant
free_agents.outlook: Pat Bryant caught all three of his targets for 47 yards in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers, but an ankle sprain knocked him out of the contest early. The second-year wide receiver is expected to miss multiple weeks, but Denver hasn't placed him on IR yet. In Bryant's absence, Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin will get more work behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton, beginning with a Week 5 matchup against a Chargers secondary that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: DeMario Douglas
free_agents.outlook: DeMario Douglas hasn't emerged in the Patriots' receiving corps ahead of a Week 5 matchup against the Raiders. Despite A.J. Brown's continued absence, Douglas has just four total catches over the last three weeks, tallying 62 yards. An uptick in volume appears unlikely against an exploitable secondary that allows 8.2 yards per target, leaving Douglas as a dart throw as opposed to a reliable lineup option.

free_agents.name: Zachariah Branch
free_agents.outlook: Zachariah Branch's offensive role could continue to grow in the Falcons' Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Branch has received two targets in each of his last three games, even out-targeting Olamide Zaccheaus over the last two weeks (four to three). Additionally, Branch played a career-high 23% of the Falcons' offensive snaps in the Week 4 win over the Saints, suggesting his offensive role may be growing. He's also in for a favorable Week 5 matchup against a Ravens secondary that's given up 734 receiving yards to wideouts through four contests this season, the sixth-most in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Kimani Vidal
free_agents.outlook: Kimani Vidal is coming off his most productive game of 2026, taking five carries for 25 yards and turning three targets into a 2-11-1 line during the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks. While the seven touches represented a season high for Vidal, they still trailed Keaton Mitchell's 15 and Omarion Hampton's 11. Mitchell led the trio with 63 scrimmage yards, while Hampton scored a rushing TD. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is drifting toward a full-blown committee as he searches for a spark, but it would likely take an injury ahead of him for Vidal to gain significant volume on a consistent basis. He'll try to build on last week's effort in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Andy Borregales
free_agents.outlook: Andy Borregales' opportunities have been scant for the Patriots ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Raiders. After not attempting an extra point in Week 3, Borregales drilled three extra points but did not attempt a field goal for the first time this season in Week 4. Las Vegas has allowed the second-fewest points to opposing kickers, surrendering 10 PATs but only five field goal tries through four games, and though the Patriots' offense may be righting its early-season struggles, Borregales has yet to regain fantasy trust.

free_agents.name: Darnell Washington
free_agents.outlook: Darnell Washington and the Steelers host the Colts in a matchup between 2-2 teams in Week 5. In Week 4, he played 70% of offensive snaps and caught three of five targets for 27 yards and a touchdown. Fellow tight end Pat Freiermuth (3-17-1) was also productive, playing 75% of the offensive snaps during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss. They're both listed as starting tight ends for the Steelers, and it looks like they'll have a nearly even snap split as long as they're healthy. Indianapolis allows 13.7 fantasy points per game to TEs, which ranks 17th.
